purpose: Register and inspect Neo Abstract Accounts against the shared AA core (UnifiedSmartWalletV3).

journeys.name: Inspect account state
journeys.detail: Account id (hash/seed) -> dispatch inspect -> chain.read getVerifier/getHook/getBackupOwner on aaCore (verified against live UnifiedSmartWalletV3 ABI) -> detail grid with hasInspected flag and empty-verifier hint. Works, but the displayed hashes come back byte-reversed (little-endian) via the shared parser so they never match the 0x big-endian hashes the user typed, and seed-derived ids essentially never correspond to a registered account because V3 ids are registration-parameter hashes (see register journey).

journeys.name: Register a new AA account shell
journeys.detail: Form -> dispatch register -> chain.invoke registerAccount(accountId, verifier, params, hook, backupOwner, timelock). The contract enforces accountId == computeRegistrationAccountId(verifier, params, hook, backupOwner, timelock): live test-invoke on testnet aborts with 'Account id does not match registration parameters'. The app derives accountId as ripemd160(sha256(seed)) (deriveAAAccountIdHash), which can never equal the registration hash, so every register attempt reverts after the wallet prompt. Even before that, the contract aborts 'Backup owner witness required' unless the backup owner signs — the app never tells the user this.

journeys.name: Derive the correct registration account id
journeys.detail: The contract exposes computeRegistrationAccountId and the repo has the exact matching JS (deriveRegistrationAccountIdHash — verified byte-for-byte against the contract via RPC: JS 5dacc04b… == reversed on-chain cbfb8e17…), but no app calls it and the UI offers no way to derive/preview the only accountId that the contract will accept.

journeys.name: Connect wallet
journeys.detail: dispatch connect -> chain.ensureWallet via notify.guard with success/error toasts.

confirmed_high.title: Register always reverts: accountId derived from seed instead of registration parameters
confirmed_high.evidence: submitRegister sends accountId = deriveAAAccountIdHash(seed) (ripemd160/sha256 of free text), but live test-invoke of registerAccount on testnet aaCore 0xdbf38e7b… aborts: 'Account id does not match registration parameters'. The contract requires accountId == computeRegistrationAccountId(verifier, verifierParams, hook, backupOwner, escapeTimelock). deriveRegistrationAccountIdHash in apps/shared/utils/aa-account.ts:110 matches the contract exactly (verified via RPC) yet is imported by no app.
confirmed_high.fix: In submitRegister, compute accountId via deriveRegistrationAccountIdHash({verifierContractHash, verifierParamsHex, hookContractHash, backupOwnerAddress, escapeTimelock}) (hex-encode the user's seed into verifierParams the way custom-anchor's buildAnchorAgentVerifierParam does), show the derived id read-only above the Register CTA, and reuse it for the post-register inspect.

confirmed_high.title: Backup-owner witness requirement is invisible until an opaque on-chain abort
confirmed_high.evidence: Live test-invoke without the backup-owner signer aborts 'Backup owner witness required'. normalizeBackupOwner accepts any valid address/hash; nothing checks it equals the connected wallet, and the hint copy ('Required recovery owner as a Neo address or script hash') invites entering a third-party address that guarantees a witness failure.
confirmed_high.fix: Prefill backupOwner with chain.address on connect; if the entered value differs from the connected wallet, block submit with a localized message ('the backup owner must sign this transaction — connect that wallet or use your own address').

medium_low.title: Inspected verifier/hook/owner display as byte-reversed hex (or garbage text)
medium_low.evidence: chain.read -> parseInvokeResult -> parseByteLike hex-encodes the raw little-endian Hash160 bytes (and even returns printable-ASCII text when all 20 bytes are printable). The 'Current Verifier' card therefore shows the reversed form of the 0x hash the user entered/sees in the hero (e.g. registering 0x7147f9a5… displays as 0x7f227cde…), making before/after comparison impossible.
medium_low.fix: Add a parseHash160 helper that base64-decodes, reverses bytes and 0x-prefixes; use it in inspectAccount for the three reads (shared issue — fix once in shared utils, most visible here and in aa-permissions-lab).

medium_low.title: No confirmation or auto-refresh after register
medium_low.evidence: submitRegister resolves on wallet broadcast; success toast 'Register transaction submitted' fires but the inspector keeps stale/empty state until the user manually re-inspects, and a FAULTed execution is never surfaced.
medium_low.fix: After invoke, poll getVerifier(accountId) (3-5 attempts, ~5s apart) and flip the inspector to the fresh state, or surface 'pending confirmation' until the read returns non-empty.

medium_low.title: Inspector omits escape timelock and escape status that registration itself configures
medium_low.evidence: The form makes the user choose an escapeTimelock (7-90 days validated) but inspect only reads verifier/hook/backupOwner; getEscapeTimelock and isEscapeActive exist in the live ABI and are never read, so the recovery posture the app is about cannot be verified.
medium_low.fix: Add getEscapeTimelock + isEscapeActive to the Promise.all in inspectAccount and render two more detail cards (timelock humanized to days).

purpose: Create, manage, and settle trustless escrow listings for Neo Abstract Account addresses.

journeys.name: Load market listings
journeys.detail: Paste market hash -> loadListings -> getListingCount + chunked getListing reads (cap 200, newest-first, truncation notice) -> cards with status/mine/pending chips. Verified against live AAAddressMarket ABI; mainnet market currently has 0 listings. Friction: the market hash starts EMPTY even though the canonical contract is in the app's own manifest and registry — a first-time user has no idea what to paste.

journeys.name: Create listing (sell an AA address)
journeys.detail: Validated form -> createListing with CustomContracts signer over [market, aaCore]. Args match the live ABI. But live test-invoke shows createListing aborts 'Account not found' unless the accountId is a registered AA account (with the seller as owner) — the app does no pre-check, so most attempts end in a raw revert after the wallet prompt. Works for users who already own a registered AA shell.

journeys.name: Update price / cancel listing
journeys.detail: Gated on selectedListing.isMine && status==='active'; updateListingPrice/cancelListing args verified against ABI; refresh after write.

journeys.name: Buy listing
journeys.detail: invokeMultiple atomically: GAS.transfer(buyer -> market, priceRaw) + settleListing(id, buyer, newBackupOwner) in one tx; newBackupOwner prefilled with the buyer's wallet; matches ABI.

journeys.name: Refund pending payment (exit path)
journeys.detail: getPendingPaymentOf fan-out per listing; 'pending refund' chip + Refund button -> refundPendingPayment(listingId, payer). Money-out path exists and is discoverable.

confirmed_high.title: Market contract hash must be hand-pasted although the app's manifest declares it
confirmed_high.evidence: loadAll only restores marketHash from localStorage cache; first run shows an empty board with 'Enter an AA market contract hash in the operation panel' — but the canonical hash is already in neo-manifest.json contracts (mainnet 0xae7afe3a…, testnet 0x8dbd4cf6…) and EXTERNAL_INTEGRATIONS.contracts.aaAddressMarket. aaContractHash gets a default (getDefaultAAContractHash) while marketHash does not.
confirmed_high.fix: Default marketHash to the manifest contract for the active network (same pattern as getDefaultAAContractHash, reading getExternalIntegrationConfig().contracts.aaAddressMarket with manifest fallback) and keep the input as an advanced override.

medium_low.title: Listing status values render as raw English in both locales
medium_low.evidence: {listing.status} and ManageListingCard.tsx:37 print the LISTING_STATUS strings 'active'/'sold'/'cancelled'/'unknown' directly; zh users see untranslated English in the most prominent chip.
medium_low.fix: Add statusActive/statusSold/statusCancelled/statusUnknown keys to locale/messages.ts and render t(`status${capitalize(listing.status)}`) while keeping the raw value for the CSS modifier.

medium_low.title: Create listing has no AA-account precondition check; reverts surface raw
medium_low.evidence: Live test-invoke of createListing with an unregistered accountId aborts 'Account not found' (AA core lookup). The accountIdHint only says 'Paste the 20-byte Account ID hash'; the user pays a failed-tx fee or gets an opaque abort for an account they don't own.
medium_low.fix: Before invoking, chain.read aaCore.getBackupOwner(accountIdHash); if empty -> localized 'this account is not registered in AA core'; if != connected wallet -> 'only the account owner can list this address'.

medium_low.title: Post-write refresh races RPC node lag — new listing often invisible until manual reload
medium_low.evidence: runWriteAction awaits the wallet txid then immediately calls loadListings(); on Neo N3 the next read usually hits a node that has not executed the tx yet, so after 'Listing created' the board still shows the old state with no pending indicator.
medium_low.fix: Poll getListingCount (create) or the affected getListing (price/cancel/buy/refund) until the value changes or ~15s timeout before reloading, mirroring the shared waitForDepositConfirmation pattern, and show a 'confirming…' status row meanwhile.

medium_low.title: One shared isSubmitting flag spins all four manage buttons simultaneously
medium_low.evidence: Update Price, Cancel, Buy and Refund all bind loading={isSubmitting}; pressing any one shows four spinners, hiding which action is in flight.
medium_low.fix: Split into per-action observables (isUpdatingPrice, isCancelling, isBuying, isRefunding) or pass the in-flight action name and only spin the matching button.

medium_low.title: createdAt/updatedAt decoded but never shown
medium_low.evidence: decodeListing parses both timestamps into the MarketListing model, but ListingCard renders no time context, so buyers cannot judge listing freshness.
medium_low.fix: Render a relative 'listed/updated X ago' line in ListingCard from the existing fields.

medium_low.title: Accent hue drifts: violet pending-chip and violet hero gradient against green tokens
medium_low.evidence: .chip--pending uses #6d4fd7 / rgba(139,92,246) violet and PlayArea.scss hero gradient ends at #f6f4ff, while the badge/eyebrow use the green --ns-violet-strong (#0fb174) tokens — two accent hues on one screen.
medium_low.fix: Restyle .chip--pending and the hero gradient endpoint with the green --ns-* token family (e.g. #E4F8F0/#0FB174) to keep a single accent hue.

purpose: Inspect and update verifier / hook bindings for Neo Abstract Accounts.

journeys.name: Inspect account permissions
journeys.detail: 40-hex account id -> refresh -> getVerifier/getHook/getBackupOwner (verified against live ABI) -> detail rows with em-dash placeholders. Works; same shared byte-reversed hash display caveat as aa-account-lab.

journeys.name: Update verifier (rotate signing policy)
journeys.detail: Form -> updateVerifier(accountId, newVerifier, params) matches the ABI and submits — but UnifiedSmartWalletV3 uses a propose->timelock->confirm flow (confirmVerifierUpdate / hasPendingVerifierUpdate / getPendingVerifierUpdateTime / cancelVerifierUpdate all in the live ABI). The app immediately re-reads state, which still shows the OLD verifier, with no pending indicator: the user sees 'update submitted' then apparently nothing happened, and the rotation can never be finalized in this app.

journeys.name: Update hook
journeys.detail: Same two-phase pattern (confirmHookUpdate / hasPendingHookUpdate in ABI); app only proposes and never confirms.

journeys.name: Confirm or cancel a pending update
journeys.detail: No UI calls confirmVerifierUpdate/confirmHookUpdate/cancelVerifierUpdate/cancelHookUpdate, so the second half of the app's core promise ('update bindings') is not reachable.

confirmed_high.title: Two-phase verifier/hook rotation cannot be completed: no confirm/cancel/pending UI
confirmed_high.evidence: submitVerifier/submitHook call only updateVerifier/updateHook then refreshState — but the live aaCore ABI (0x0268a387… mainnet) has confirmVerifierUpdate, confirmHookUpdate, cancelVerifierUpdate, cancelHookUpdate, hasPendingVerifierUpdate, getPendingVerifierUpdateTime. The post-submit read shows the unchanged old verifier, so the success toast ('Verifier update submitted') is followed by visibly stale state and the rotation is never finalizable here.
confirmed_high.fix: Extend refreshState to also read hasPendingVerifierUpdate/hasPendingHookUpdate + getPending*UpdateTime; when pending, render a banner with the unlock countdown and Confirm / Cancel buttons dispatching confirmVerifierUpdate / cancelVerifierUpdate (and hook equivalents).

medium_low.title: 'configured' status chip appears as soon as any account id is typed, before any read
medium_low.evidence: {accountReady ? {t('configured')} : null} keys purely off accountIdHash.trim(); typing 40 junk hex chars shows a green 'configured' badge above three em-dash placeholder rows — the chip asserts state that was never fetched.
medium_low.fix: Add a hasInspected observable (set true after a successful refreshState, like aa-account-lab) and gate the chip on it; show 'not inspected' otherwise.

medium_low.title: No authorization pre-check or guidance for who may rotate bindings
medium_low.evidence: chain.invoke updateVerifier is sent with the connected wallet as the only signer; the contract enforces account-owner authorization (registration enforces backup-owner witness; live probe on unregistered ids aborts 'Account not found'). Nothing checks the connected wallet equals getBackupOwner(accountId), so unauthorized users hit raw ABORTMSG text after signing.
medium_low.fix: After a successful inspect, compare currentBackupOwner with the connected wallet hash and disable the write CTAs with a localized 'connect the backup-owner wallet to rotate this account' hint when they differ.

medium_low.title: Hash160 reads display byte-reversed (shared parser)
medium_low.evidence: formatPermissionValue(String(...)) renders parseByteLike output: little-endian hex of the verifier/hook/owner, which never matches the canonical 0x form the user enters in the update fields directly below — verifying a rotation by eye is impossible.
medium_low.fix: Decode with a byte-reversing hash160 parser (same shared fix as aa-account-lab) so reads and write inputs share one canonical format.

medium_low.title: Success copy claims completion for what is only a proposal
medium_low.evidence: successVerifier 'Verifier update submitted' / successHook 'Hook update submitted' read as final; combined with the unchanged refresh the user cannot tell the update is pending a timelock confirm.
medium_low.fix: Reword to 'Verifier update proposed — confirm after the timelock' (en+zh) once the pending UI from the first finding lands.

purpose: Check paymaster sponsorship and submit relay-ready payloads through the shared Neo AA relay.

journeys.name: Check sponsorship
journeys.detail: AA address -> checkSponsor -> AAService.checkSponsorship -> GET /api/rpc/gas-sponsor-check. Live probe today against the production host (neomini.app) returns {"error":{"code":"FORBIDDEN","message":"function not allowed"}} — the host's EDGE_RPC_ALLOWLIST does not include the gas-sponsor functions, so despite the oracle/edge infra being back, this journey still fails before reaching it.

journeys.name: Request sponsorship
journeys.detail: POST /api/rpc/gas-sponsor-request — same allowlist block as the check journey (FORBIDDEN at the host proxy, pages/api/rpc/[fn].ts isEdgeRpcAllowed).

journeys.name: Submit relay payload
journeys.detail: POST /api/aa/relay live-probed: {"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"AA_RELAY_URL (or NEXT_PUBLIC_AA_RELAY_URL) not configured"}} — the host deployment has no relay upstream configured. The app-side flow (JSON validation, paymaster scope injection, normalizeRelayResult accepting txid/accepted statuses) is sound but can never reach a relay.

journeys.name: Compose and validate a payload
journeys.detail: JSON validity gates the submit button with inline hints; but the default payload only contains metaInvocation.scriptHash with no operation/args, so even with a live relay the canned example would be rejected upstream.

confirmed_high.title: All three journeys still dead in production: host proxy blocks gas-sponsor functions and AA_RELAY_URL is unset
confirmed_high.evidence: Live probes (2026-06-12): GET https://neomini.app/api/rpc/gas-sponsor-check?... -> {"error":{"code":"FORBIDDEN","message":"function not allowed"}} (isEdgeRpcAllowed: EDGE_RPC_ALLOWLIST entries exclude it); POST https://neomini.app/api/aa/relay -> 'AA_RELAY_URL (or NEXT_PUBLIC_AA_RELAY_URL) not configured'. The oracle restoration did not update the host deployment env, so the app remains 100% non-functional for users.
confirmed_high.fix: Add gas-sponsor-check and gas-sponsor-request to EDGE_RPC_ALLOWLIST and set AA_RELAY_URL (pointing at the restored relay) in the production host environment; add a smoke test that fails deploys when these two endpoints return FORBIDDEN/unconfigured.

confirmed_high.title: Raw server JSON leaks into user-facing error toasts
confirmed_high.evidence: requestJson throws new Error(text) with the verbatim response body, so notify.guard toasts the literal string {"error":{"code":"FORBIDDEN","message":"function not allowed"}} — unreadable and untranslated (shared issue, most visible here; also hits aa-session-key-lab).
confirmed_high.fix: In requestJson, try JSON.parse(text) and throw error.error?.message ?? error.message ?? text; map known codes (FORBIDDEN, INTERNAL_ERROR) to localized 'sponsorship service unavailable' copy at the app layer.

medium_low.title: Sponsor-check result headline hides eligibility and remaining quota
medium_low.evidence: The result line only inspects error/message/status keys; SponsorshipStatus.eligible, remaining, dailyLimit, usedToday are never rendered as a summary — the actual answer to 'am I sponsored?' is buried in the collapsed raw-JSON <details>.
medium_low.fix: When the result has an `eligible` field, render 'Eligible — {remaining} GAS of {dailyLimit} remaining today' (or a red 'Not eligible: {reason}') as the headline instead of the generic 'Sponsor check complete.'

medium_low.title: Default relay payload is not a submittable example
medium_low.evidence: getDefaultRelayPayload emits {"metaInvocation":{"scriptHash":aaCore}} with no operation/args/signature fields, so the one-click happy path submits a payload the relay must reject — bad first-run experience for a console meant to demonstrate the relay.
medium_low.fix: Ship a complete sample metaInvocation (scriptHash + operation: 'getNonce', args: [accountId, 0]) or annotate required fields in payloadJsonHint.

medium_low.title: AA address input accepts anything; no Neo-address validation before enabling actions
medium_low.evidence: canCheckSponsor only requires aaAddress.trim() truthy; 'abc' enables all three actions and fails server-side.
medium_low.fix: Validate with the shared isHash160OrNeoAddress-style check (as aa-market-hub does) and show an inline error on the input.

purpose: Configure a scoped SessionKeyVerifier on-chain and inspect AA sponsorship state.

journeys.name: Generate session key pair
journeys.detail: generateAASessionKeyPair (p256) -> public key auto-fills the form; private key shown masked with reveal toggle and clipboard copy incl. insecure-context failure handling. Good security UX.

journeys.name: Configure session key on-chain
journeys.detail: Form -> aaCore.callVerifier(accountId, 'setSessionKey', [accountId, pubKey, target, method, expiresAt]) — 5 inner args. Live ABI check: mainnet SessionKeyVerifier 0x3ba83334… requires SEVEN params (adds spendingLimit:Integer, description:String) while the testnet deploy still has the old 5-param signature. Default network is mainnet, so the forwarded contract call arity-mismatches and faults every time. Additionally the accountId is seed-derived (same V3 registration-hash mismatch as aa-account-lab), so the target account is almost never registered ('Account not found').

journeys.name: Inspect the active session key
journeys.detail: The verifier exposes getSessionKey/getSessionKeyMetadata/getSpentAmount (live ABI) but the app never reads them; the 'Latest state' panel echoes local form values only.

journeys.name: Revoke a session key
journeys.detail: clearSessionKey(accountId) exists on the verifier but no UI exposes it — a permission-granting tool with no permission-out path.

journeys.name: Check / request sponsorship
journeys.detail: Same production host endpoints as aa-relay-console: /api/rpc/gas-sponsor-check returns FORBIDDEN 'function not allowed' (live-verified today). See aa-relay-console for the primary finding.

confirmed_high.title: Configure faults on mainnet: setSessionKey called with 5 args but mainnet verifier requires 7
confirmed_high.evidence: configureSessionKey forwards [accountId, pubKey, targetContract, method, expiresAt] via callVerifier. Live ABI: mainnet SessionKeyVerifier 0x3ba83334… setSessionKey(accountId, pubKey, targetContract, method, validUntil, spendingLimit, description) — 7 params; testnet 0xed44c885… still has the old 5-param version. With default_network=mainnet the inner contract call arity-mismatches and the tx faults after the user signs.
confirmed_high.fix: Append { type: 'Integer', value: spendingLimit (default '0' = unlimited or a UI input) } and { type: 'String', value: description } to the args array; ideally read the verifier's contract manifest at startup and branch on parameter count so testnet keeps working.

confirmed_high.title: No revoke or on-chain inspect: clearSessionKey/getSessionKey never wired
confirmed_high.evidence: The live verifier ABI has clearSessionKey, getSessionKey, getSessionKeyMetadata and getSpentAmount; the app exposes none, so a user who delegated signing authority cannot see or revoke it here — the security-critical exit path is missing.
confirmed_high.fix: Add an 'Active session' card: chain.read getSessionKey(accountId) on the session verifier to show key/target/method/expiry/spent, plus a Revoke button dispatching callVerifier(accountId, 'clearSessionKey', [accountId]).

confirmed_high.title: Status flips to 'Configured' on broadcast with zero on-chain verification
confirmed_high.evidence: lastConfigured is set from the local form as soon as invokeContract returns a txid; no application-log check or getSessionKey readback. Combined with the mainnet arity fault, every mainnet user sees a green 'Configured' hero metric and a full detail list for a session key that does not exist.
confirmed_high.fix: After the invoke, poll the tx application log for HALT (or read getSessionKey until it returns the new pubKey) before setting lastConfigured; on FAULT show the VM exception via notify.

medium_low.title: Seed-derived account id is almost never a registered account; no precondition check
medium_low.evidence: deriveAAAccountIdHash(seed) does not match V3 registration ids (registration binds id to computeRegistrationAccountId — proven live in aa-account-lab review), and callVerifier on an unknown id aborts 'Account not found'. The default seed 'neo-aa-001' guarantees this failure for first-time users.
medium_low.fix: Before configure, chain.read aaCore.getVerifier(accountId); if empty, block with 'no AA account registered at this id — register one first' (deeplink neomainapp://aa-account-lab); also accept a literal 0x account id like the other labs.

medium_low.title: Hardcoded English eyebrow 'Session Keys'
medium_low.evidence: Session Keys bypasses t(); every other string in the app (92 en/zh pairs) is localized.
medium_low.fix: Add sessionHeroEyebrow {en:'Session Keys', zh:'会话密钥'} to locale/messages.ts and render t('sessionHeroEyebrow').

medium_low.title: Expiry must be typed as a raw unix timestamp
medium_low.evidence: expiresAt is a plain text input with placeholder 'Unix timestamp'; the default helps, but changing the window requires epoch arithmetic and an invalid value only errors at submit (invalidExpiry).
medium_low.fix: Render quick-pick chips (+1h/+24h/+7d) that write the computed epoch, plus a humanized preview line ('expires 2026-06-13 14:00') under the input.

purpose: Build Morpheus compute request previews that keep sealed inputs redacted before a later dispatch step.

journeys.name: Build a compute preview (workflow + privacy + input)
journeys.detail: Select workflow/privacy, paste input JSON, Build Preview -> buildResult (appConfig.ts:90) computes FNV digests locally, rows render, lastStatus/lastDigest/requestCount observables update via shared runPreview (ConsoleToolPanel.tsx:127-147), success toast fires. Sealed mode genuinely omits raw input from the payload (inputPreview '[sealed input redacted]') as promised.

journeys.name: Copy payload / Reset
journeys.detail: Copy uses services.clipboard.copy with localized 'copied' toast; Reset restores the exact seeded placeholders and zeroes the session counter (ConsoleToolPanel.tsx:149-159).

journeys.name: Dispatch the prepared compute job to the live Morpheus worker
journeys.detail: Payload hardcodes execution:'preview_only', dispatchReady:false (appConfig.ts:104-105) and there is no submit path. The restored mainnet worker now advertises compute_merged_into_oracle + oracle/query + oracle/smart-fetch lanes (verified live at oracle.meshmini.app/mainnet/health), so the business model's second half (run the compute) has no in-app continuation, not even a link.

journeys.name: Seal compute input for confidential handling (host operation panel)
journeys.detail: neo-manifest.json operation_panel routes sealOracleRequest/buildOraclePackage to the host-side PlayAreaOracle which does real X25519-HKDF-AES-GCM sealing; works, but it is a separate surface from the embedded console and nothing in the console explains the relationship.

confirmed_high.title: All five preview consoles have no path to the now-live oracle (shared panel is sync-only)
confirmed_high.evidence: ConsoleToolConfig.buildResult is a synchronous (values,t)=>ConsoleResult (ConsoleToolPanel.tsx:48-51); runPreview (line 127) only computes a local FNV-1a previewId. Verified live: https://oracle.meshmini.app/mainnet/health returns runtime:'nitro-worker' with oracle/query, oracle/smart-fetch, feeds/price, vrf/random, neodid/* lanes — yet every console payload says dispatchReady:false. SHARED finding, reported once here; applies to compute-lab, http, neodid, seal, vrf consoles.
confirmed_high.fix: Extend ConsoleToolConfig with an optional async dispatch(values) => Promise<ConsoleResult> and a secondary 'Send to oracle (live)' button (loading state + error toast via notify.guardResult). Each console then maps to its live lane: compute->oracle/query, http->oracle/smart-fetch dry-run, vrf->vrf/random, neodid->neodid/providers, price symbol->feeds/price/:symbol. Keep the existing preview as step 1.

medium_low.title: Console pinned to 'Morpheus Testnet' — the lane that is still degraded
medium_low.evidence: appMeta.networkLabel hardcodes 'Morpheus Testnet' (appConfig.ts:9) and neo-manifest.json:24-27 declares supported_networks/default_network neo-n3-testnet only. Verified live: oracle.meshmini.app/testnet/health still returns runtime:'emergency-vercel-runtime', degraded:true, while /mainnet is the restored nitro worker. The hero advertises the one network where Morpheus compute is NOT live.
medium_low.fix: Add neo-n3-mainnet to supported_networks and derive networkLabel from getNetwork() instead of a hardcoded string, so the console reflects the actually-live lane.

medium_low.title: Input payload accepts any garbage with no JSON validity feedback
medium_low.evidence: buildResult (appConfig.ts:90-131) digests whatever string is in 'input' with no validation; sibling consoles validate (seal console JSON.parse check appConfig.ts:85-90; http console URL scheme check). Default value is JSON, placeholder is JSON, but a typo'd payload silently previews as 'Compute preview ready'.
medium_low.fix: Mirror the seal console: try JSON.parse(input), add an 'Input is valid JSON: Yes/No' row, and set payload.status='input_required' (or at least a warning status) when invalid so the shared panel classifies it as a warning.

medium_low.title: zh summaries interpolate raw English enum values
medium_low.evidence: computeSummary zh = '{workflow} {privacy} 预览已准备' (appConfig.ts:157) is interpolated with raw values 'risk-score'/'sealed' (line 123), producing mixed-language strings like 'risk-score sealed 预览已准备'. Localized labels exist (workflowRisk, privacySealed) but are not used.
medium_low.fix: Resolve the selected option's labelKey through t() before interpolating: t('computeSummary', { workflow: t(optionLabelKey), privacy: t(privacyLabelKey) }).

medium_low.title: Digest stat seeded with 'N/A' instead of em-dash
medium_low.evidence: main.tsx:17 seeds lastDigest with ctx.t('notAvailable') which is 'N/A' (base-messages.ts:27). The seal console already fixed this with a digestPlaceholder '—' key; the shared panel's Reset deliberately restores whatever the app seeded.
medium_low.fix: Add digestPlaceholder: { en: '—', zh: '—' } to appMessages and seed lastDigest with ctx.t('digestPlaceholder'), matching oracle-seal-console.

medium_low.title: Shared console eyebrow/labels drop the Neo Soft uppercase+tracking system
medium_low.evidence: Eyebrow and all micro-labels are styled with letter-spacing:0 and no text-transform (ConsoleToolPanel.scss:60-65, 99-104, 399-405), unlike the platform's eyebrow recipe (uppercase + .12em tracking, cf. price console .price-eyebrow PlayArea.scss:60-66). Hero h2 also has letter-spacing:0 instead of the negative tracking used on big figures. SHARED, most visible in the three consoles with no app-level SCSS (compute-lab, neodid, seal).
medium_low.fix: In the shared SCSS set .console-tool__eyebrow { text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.12em; font-size: 11px; } and .console-tool__intro h2 { letter-spacing: -0.02em; }; apply the same treatment to row/payload micro-labels.

purpose: Prepare HTTP oracle reads (method, URL, JSON path, body) before binding them to an on-chain callback.

journeys.name: Build an HTTP request preview with URL validation
journeys.detail: Method/URL/jsonPath/body -> buildResult validates http(s) scheme (appConfig.ts:84-90); invalid URL is classified payload.status='input_required' so the shared panel shows a warning toast, preserves the digest placeholder and does not increment Requests (appConfig.ts:103-117 + ConsoleToolPanel.tsx:130-146). This is the best-engineered validation flow in the cluster.

journeys.name: POST request with body
journeys.detail: Body is only folded into the digest/payload for POST (appConfig.ts:81), correctly representing what would be bound on-chain; GET bodies are dropped.

journeys.name: Copy payload / Reset
journeys.detail: Standard shared panel behavior; reset restores seeded placeholders.

purpose: Query live Morpheus price feed values (NEO/GAS/BTC vs USD) directly from the on-chain MorpheusDataFeed contract.

journeys.name: Fetch a live price
journeys.detail: Fetch Price -> dispatch('fetchPrice') -> usePriceConsole.fetchPrice -> useMorpheusDataFeed.getPrice -> invokefunction getLatest('TWELVEDATA:NEO-USD') on 0x03013f49...ccab via api.n3index.dev/mainnet. Verified live today: HALT, price 2.181, dataTimestamp = today (feed restored and updating). Result renders in the balance card with loading state on the button and exactly one correct toast (main.tsx:35-46 deliberately branches on the result instead of notify.guard — good).

journeys.name: Switch asset and re-fetch
journeys.detail: NeoSelect -> dispatch('updateAsset') -> price.asset.set; hero pair, token badge and colors react. Deep-link ?asset=GAS is sanitized through launchAsset (main.tsx:13-22).

journeys.name: Judge how fresh the displayed price is
journeys.detail: getLatest returns dataTimestamp in field [1], but the hook discards it and returns only fields[2] (useMorpheusDataFeed.ts:121-132). The UI then shows the green 'Fresh feed result' badge for ANY successful read (PlayArea.tsx:80-86). On testnet — which the manifest also supports — the feed is verifiably frozen at 2026-03-09 (confirmed via RPC today), yet the console would label that 3-month-old price 'Fresh'.

journeys.name: Discover all available feed pairs
journeys.detail: The live catalog has 20+ pairs (ETH, SOL, TRX, PAXG, WTI, BRENT, commodities — verified via /mainnet/feeds/catalog) and the hook already implements listPairs() (useMorpheusDataFeed.ts:140-159), but the UI hardcodes a 3-option select (PlayArea.tsx:99-103), so most of the product's data is invisible.

confirmed_high.title: Feed timestamp discarded — stale prices labeled 'Fresh feed result'
confirmed_high.evidence: getLatest's struct is [pair, dataTimestamp, price, recordTimestamp, signature, flag] (comment at useMorpheusDataFeed.ts:113) but getPrice reads only fields[2] (lines 121-128) and returns a bare number; PlayArea.tsx:85 then renders t('priceStatusLive') = 'Fresh feed result' for any HALT. Verified: testnet feed (0x9bea75cf...) still returns 2026-03-09 data — this UI would call it fresh. This is exactly the failure mode that hid the 3-month feed freeze.
confirmed_high.fix: Return { price, timestamp } from getPrice; in the console render 'as of <relative time>' next to the price and flip the badge to a warning state (e.g. amber 'Stale feed — last update 94 days ago') when now - dataTimestamp exceeds a threshold (e.g. 1h).

medium_low.title: Only 3 of 20+ live feed pairs are selectable; listPairs() unused

medium_low.fix: On mount, call listPairs() (or keep the trio as instant defaults and lazily extend) and populate the select from the on-chain catalog; keep launchAsset's allowlist in sync by validating against the fetched list.

purpose: Package sensitive oracle input as a sealed-envelope preview with a reference checksum.

journeys.name: Build an envelope preview
journeys.detail: Purpose/recipient/payload -> buildResult validates JSON.parse (appConfig.ts:85-90), shows a 'Payload is valid JSON' row, and computes payload + envelope checksums. The sensitive payload is correctly NEVER echoed into the result payload (only payloadValid + digests, appConfig.ts:104-113) — good privacy hygiene. In-app copy is admirably honest: 'non-cryptographic reference checksum (not encryption)' (appConfig.ts:124-126, feature1Desc).

journeys.name: Copy payload / Reset
journeys.detail: Works; this is the one console that seeds the digest stat with the proper '—' placeholder (main.tsx:17 uses digestPlaceholder), which Reset faithfully restores.

journeys.name: Actually encrypt/seal the payload
journeys.detail: In-app, sealing never happens — only a checksum. Real X25519-HKDF-AES-GCM sealing exists but only on the host operation-panel surface (PlayAreaOracle sealOracleRequest, with Morpheus store refs). With the worker's oracle/public-key lane live again, the in-app builder still cannot do the thing the app is named after. Covered by the shared sync-only finding under oracle-compute-lab.

medium_low.title: Two 'Seal' surfaces with contradictory promises: manifest says encrypt, app says not-encryption
medium_low.evidence: operation_panel copy promises 'Seal sensitive oracle input and inspect the encrypted reference' / 'Encrypt a sensitive payload for Morpheus confidential handling' (neo-manifest.json:53,58) — accurate only for the host-side sealOracleRequest path — while the embedded console's own description says 'non-cryptographic reference checksum (not encryption)' (appConfig.ts:124-126). A user cannot tell which 'Build Envelope' button actually protects their data.
medium_low.fix: Now that the mainnet worker's oracle/public-key lane is live, wire the in-app builder to the same client-side seal (fetch oracle public key, X25519-HKDF-AES-GCM in-browser, output secret_ref/ciphertext) so both surfaces match; otherwise rename the in-app action to 'Build reference envelope' and add one sentence pointing at the host Seal Payload operation for real encryption.

medium_low.title: Console pinned to the degraded testnet lane
medium_low.evidence: appMeta.networkLabel hardcodes 'Morpheus Testnet' (appConfig.ts:9); neo-manifest.json:24-27 testnet-only. The privacy_oracle and oracle/decrypt lanes are live on mainnet only; testnet still reports privacy_oracle:false, degraded:true (verified live).
medium_low.fix: Add neo-n3-mainnet support and derive the network label from getNetwork().

medium_low.title: Invalid-JSON preview still counts as success (inconsistent with http console)
medium_low.evidence: When JSON.parse fails, the result keeps a success classification — payload has no status:'input_required' (appConfig.ts:104-113) — so the green toast fires, Requests increments, and lastDigest updates, while the row simultaneously says 'Payload is valid JSON: No'. The http sibling classifies its analogous URL failure as input_required so the panel warns.
medium_low.fix: If the field's contract is 'private JSON payload', spread { status: 'input_required' } into the payload on parse failure (exactly the http console pattern at oracle-http-console/src/appConfig.ts:110) so toast/counter/digest stay honest; keep the row for explanation.

medium_low.title: Empty recipient renders a blank result row
medium_low.evidence: recipient defaults to '' and clean(values.recipient,'') passes empty through (appConfig.ts:81); the result then renders a Recipient row with an empty value (appConfig.ts:99) while '' is silently folded into the envelope checksum.
medium_low.fix: Show '—' for an empty recipient in the row, and add an explicit '(none)' marker in the payload (recipient: recipient || null) so two envelopes differing only by blank-vs-missing recipient are distinguishable.

purpose: Create NEP-17 tokens from audited on-chain templates via the platform MiniAppFactory contract — configure supply/owner/treasury/mintability without uploading artifacts.

journeys.name: configure token + generate template plan
journeys.detail: Form → dispatch('generatePlan') → buildNep17Plan validates name/symbol/decimals/supply (base-unit BigInt math, no float), owner/treasury address regex → deterministic digest+packageId → stats/sidebar update. Testnet factory contract 0x03a7c8fc… is baked into the build (verified in dist) and templateExists('tpl.nep17.asset.v1')=true on live testnet RPC. Mainnet is honestly blocked (env empty → factory_contract_not_configured).

journeys.name: sign plan with wallet
journeys.detail: signCurrentPlan → chain.signMessage over digest+packageId; correctly gated on the STORED plan (preview-ready-but-unsaved hint shown). But the signature is only displayed on screen — it is not merged into the copyable package JSON and has no copy button, so the attestation can't travel with the artifact. Digest is non-cryptographic FNV-1a-64.

journeys.name: deploy the asset (create the token)
journeys.detail: The core promise fails twice. (1) The app never executes: only generatePlan/signCurrentPlan actions exist (runtime.tsx:64-101); the checklist marks 'Deploy NEP-17 from template' as manual with no path, and neo-manifest declares transactions:false / no invoke permission. (2) Even manual submission creates nothing: live testnet getTemplate('tpl.nep17.asset.v1') returns HasArtifact=false, and MiniAppFactory.DeployFromTemplate (MiniAppFactory.cs:229-236) only deploys via ContractManagement when an artifact is preloaded — otherwise it just stores a DeploymentRecord and returns UInt160.Zero. No NEP-17 token can come into existence, while the UI claims templateArtifact.status='preloaded-on-chain'.

journeys.name: find/manage what I created afterwards
journeys.detail: Contract exposes getDeployment(packageId), deploymentCount, getDeploymentIdByIndex — the UI never reads any of them. After generate+sign there is nothing else to do in-app; 'Generated' stat is session-only and resets on reload. No 'my deployments' view exists.

journeys.name: OneGate deeplink prefill
journeys.detail: createFactoryDraftFromLaunchContext maps ?name/symbol/owner/initialSupply/decimals/network params into the draft with sanitization; oneGate.url card with copy button regenerates a prefilled launch link.

confirmed_high.title: Promise unfulfillable: on-chain template has no artifact, so no token can ever be created
confirmed_high.evidence: TEMPLATE_REGISTRY hardcodes artifact status 'preloaded-on-chain' with nef/manifest hashes, but live testnet getTemplate('tpl.nep17.asset.v1') on 0x03a7c8fc… returns HasArtifact=false; DeployFromTemplate (contracts/platform/MiniAppFactory/MiniAppFactory.cs:229) only calls ContractManagement.Deploy when HasArtifact — otherwise records and returns UInt160.Zero. The checklist tells users 'Use the preloaded NEF and manifest stored by the Factory contract', which is false on-chain.
confirmed_high.fix: Compile the real NEP-17 template contract and have the factory admin call registerTemplateArtifact('tpl.nep17.asset.v1', nef, manifest) on testnet (and mainnet when configured). Until then, derive artifact status from getTemplate() at runtime and render 'metadata-only — deployment records, does not mint' instead of 'preloaded-on-chain'.

confirmed_high.title: No execute step: the app generates a deploymentCall it never submits
confirmed_high.evidence: Only two registered actions exist (generatePlan, signCurrentPlan). plan.deploymentCall {scriptHash, operation:'deployFromTemplate', 4 String args} matches the deployed ABI exactly (verified against contracts/build/MiniAppFactory.manifest.json), and DeployFromTemplate is creator-witness gated (any user may call it) — yet the deploy checklist step stays 'manual' forever with no instructions on where to submit.
confirmed_high.fix: Add a 'Submit to factory' action: ctx.services.chain.invoke(plan.deploymentCall.operation, plan.deploymentCall.args, { scriptHash: plan.deploymentCall.scriptHash, waitForEvent: 'TokenDeployed' }), enabled when publishable; surface txid + deployed hash. Update neo-manifest permissions (add invoke) and platform.transactions:true.

confirmed_high.title: No post-creation management view despite contract support
confirmed_high.evidence: MiniAppFactory ABI exposes getDeployment(packageId), deploymentCount, getDeploymentIdByIndex — none are read. The output column has plan/checklist/OneGate cards only; users cannot verify a submitted package or list past deployments (cluster requirement: 'can they find/manage what they made?').
confirmed_high.fix: Add a 'My deployments' card: iterate getDeploymentIdByIndex/deploymentCount (or getDeployment by the locally stored packageIds), filter by creator, show templateId, digest, deployedHash with explorer link.

medium_low.title: First load opens in a red Blocked state; owner is never prefilled from the connected wallet
medium_low.evidence: DEFAULT_FACTORY_DRAFT.nep17.owner='' so the very first render shows the hero pill 'Blocked' plus the blocking error 'Owner must be a Neo N3 address or Hash160' before the user touches anything. ChainService exposes chain.address (RefCompatObservable) but FactoryPlayArea never binds it; users must paste their own address by hand.
medium_low.fix: In createFactorySetup expose chain.address into state; in FactoryPlayArea seed nep17.owner/treasury (and nep11.owner, miniapp.admin) from it when empty, plus a 'Use my address' affix button on the owner input.

medium_low.title: Validation errors, warnings, checklist steps and status pills are hardcoded English (zh users get mixed-language UI)
medium_low.evidence: Shared-component issue reported once here (most visible in factories, actual file apps/shared/factory/FactoryPlayArea.tsx:17-69 + factoryPlan.ts:339-369): ERROR_COPY/WARNING_COPY maps, networkLabel('Mainnet'), kindLabel('NEP-17 asset'), makeSteps titles/details ('Validate inputs', 'Fix blocking errors before deployment.') and the raw {step.status} ('ready'/'manual'/'blocked') bypass t() entirely, while locale/messages.ts has full en+zh parity for everything else.
medium_low.fix: Move ERROR_COPY/WARNING_COPY/step copy into apps/shared/factory/messages.ts with zh translations; render step.status via t('stepReady'/'stepManual'/'stepBlocked'); thread t into makeSteps (build steps in the component from keys rather than in factoryPlan.ts).

medium_low.title: Wallet signature is not bound into the exported package
medium_low.evidence: packageJson includes packageId/digest/template/deploymentCall/payload but omits walletSignature; the signature renders read-only at lines 370-375 with no copy button, so 'Copy template plan' after signing exports an unsigned artifact — the whole point of the signing step is lost downstream.
medium_low.fix: After signCurrentPlan succeeds, include { signature, signerAddress, signedAt } in the copied package JSON and add a copy affordance on the signature block.

medium_low.title: Signed digest is non-cryptographic FNV-1a 64-bit
medium_low.evidence: digestPayload uses FNV-1a over canonical JSON (64-bit) — collision-findable, yet docSafetyModelBody sells it as 'deterministic and signer-bound' and the wallet signature attests to it.
medium_low.fix: Compute SHA-256 via crypto.subtle.digest over the stable JSON (async, cached on the plan) and keep the short suffix for display.

medium_low.title: No GAS fee estimate anywhere in the deploy plan
medium_low.evidence: The deploy checklist and package card never mention deployment cost (a real ContractManagement.Deploy costs ~10 GAS); cluster bar explicitly asks for fee transparency in creation wizards.
medium_low.fix: Run a read-only invokefunction of the deploymentCall when publishable and render gasconsumed as 'Estimated deploy fee ≈ X GAS' in the checklist deploy step.

journeys.detail: Same shared engine as asset-factory with NEP-11-specific validation: collection name, symbol, maxSupply 1–1,000,000, royalty 0–1000bps, HTTPS base URI with trailing slash, transferable→'transferable'/'soulbound' transferPolicy. tpl.nep11.collection.v1 confirmed registered on testnet factory contract.

journeys.name: sign plan
journeys.detail: Identical to asset-factory: works but signature not exported with the package; FNV-64 digest.

journeys.name: deploy the collection (mint the NEP-11 contract)
journeys.detail: Identical root cause to asset-factory: no in-app execute action, and live testnet getTemplate shows HasArtifact=false for the NEP-11 template, so even a manual deployFromTemplate only records a DeploymentRecord — no collection contract is ever instantiated. The 'Create NEP-11 collections' promise cannot complete.

journeys.name: find/manage created collections (mint NFTs, change royalty)
journeys.detail: No deployments view (getDeployment/deploymentCount unused), and since the template never deploys there is also no follow-on mint/manage surface anywhere. The business model (creator drops, tickets, badges per docWhatItIsBody) implies a mint journey the platform cannot deliver yet.

journeys.name: OneGate deeplink prefill
journeys.detail: name/symbol/owner/maxSupply/baseUri params map into the NEP-11 draft with sanitization.

confirmed_high.title: NEP-11 template has no on-chain artifact — collection creation can never complete
confirmed_high.evidence: Same engine-level gap as asset-factory, verified independently: tpl.nep11.collection.v1 exists on testnet 0x03a7c8fc… but its HasArtifact flag is false (registerTemplate stores only hash metadata; registerTemplateArtifact never called), while the UI hardcodes status 'preloaded-on-chain' and the manifest promises 'Create NEP-11 collections'.
confirmed_high.fix: Preload the real NEP-11 collection NEF+manifest via admin registerTemplateArtifact, or surface live getTemplate().HasArtifact and downgrade the promise to 'plan and record' until artifacts ship.

confirmed_high.title: No execute or deployments view (shared engine gap)
confirmed_high.evidence: Identical to asset-factory findings 2–3: only generatePlan/signCurrentPlan actions; deploymentCall (matches deployFromTemplate ABI) never submitted; getDeployment/deploymentCount never read.
confirmed_high.fix: Same shared fix as asset-factory: add 'Submit to factory' invoke + 'My deployments' card in apps/shared/factory; both factories inherit it.

purpose: Register and manage human-readable .neo domain names (official NNS NFT contract): search, register, renew, set target address, transfer.

journeys.name: search domain availability + price
journeys.detail: Search button → isAvailable(fullName) + getPrice(length) against official NameService 0x50ac1c37… (ABI verified on mainnet AND the same hash confirmed deployed on testnet; getPrice(5)=2 GAS verified live). Result snapshot prevents register-drift when the query is edited; editing clears stale result/cost. Friction: no Enter-to-search, empty-query error toast literally says 'myname.neo', and a taken name's owner renders as little-endian 0x-hex instead of an N-address.

journeys.name: register an available domain
journeys.detail: register(name, owner) matches the official ABI; cost shown pre-invoke; waitForEvent:'Transfer'; success toast via notify.guard. BUT the post-success refresh (loadMyDomains) always returns empty (see journey 3), so the paid-for domain never appears — the user sees 'registered!' followed by 'You don't own any domains yet', which reads as a failed purchase. Registration term (1 year) is never stated; the perYear locale key exists but is unused.

journeys.name: view my domains
journeys.detail: loadMyDomains → chain.read('tokensOf') → wallet provider call → host /api/rpc/neo → invokefunction returns {'type':'InteropInterface','interface':'IIterator','id':…} (verified live against api.n3index.dev); parseStackItem returns typed.value=undefined for InteropInterface and nothing in the stack (host bridge, RPC proxy allowlist, wallet-sdk) ever traverses the iterator → tokens=[] always → 'My Domains' permanently empty regardless of holdings.

journeys.name: renew a domain
journeys.detail: renew(name) call itself matches the ABI and would work, but the only Renew button lives on domain-list rows that never render (journey 3). Additionally renew fires a paid wallet tx with zero price disclosure or confirmation.

journeys.name: set target address record
journeys.detail: setRecord(name, 16, addr) + resolve(name,16) are ABI-correct with good client-side address validation and inline field errors — but the Manage panel is only reachable via the (never-populated) domain list.

journeys.name: transfer domain
journeys.detail: NEP-11 transfer(to, tokenId, '') with tokenId=base64('name.neo') matches the on-chain token id format (verified via getnep11balances: tokenid hex '6e656f2e6e656f' = 'neo.neo') — correct code, gated behind the dead list.

confirmed_high.title: Domain list can never load: tokensOf session iterator is never traversed anywhere in the stack
confirmed_high.evidence: chain.read('tokensOf') → parseStackItem (apps/shared/utils/neo.ts:142-143) returns typed.value for InteropInterface, but live invokefunction against api.n3index.dev returns {'type':'InteropInterface','interface':'IIterator','id':'38d9cab3-…'} with no value field → undefined → tokens=[] → myDomains always empty. /api/rpc/neo ALLOWED_METHODS has no traverseiterator/terminatesession, the host bridge invokeBridgeRead returns the raw result, and dapi wallets return the same shape. Every manage journey (renew/set-target/transfer) plus the domainCount/expiringSoon stats are dead, and successful registrations look failed.
confirmed_high.fix: Add a shared iterator-aware read: build an invokescript wrapper (already allowlisted in /api/rpc/neo) that calls tokensOf then loops System.Iterator.Next packing up to ~100 items into an array; or add getnep11balances (verified working on api.n3index.dev) to ALLOWED_METHODS and read token ids from it. Keep token ids as raw base64 — parseByteLike text-decodes printable byte strings, so '.neo' names must be re-encoded before the properties/ownerOf ByteArray args.

confirmed_high.title: Post-registration state contradicts the success toast
confirmed_high.evidence: registerDomain success path clears the search and calls loadMyDomains(), which (finding 1) yields [] — the user paid 2+ GAS, saw 'registered!', and the screen shows the 'You don't own any domains yet' empty state.
confirmed_high.fix: Until the iterator fix lands, optimistically append {name: fullName, owner: addr, expiry: Date.now()+31536000000} to myDomains after the Transfer event confirms, then reconcile on the next successful loadMyDomains.

medium_low.evidence: One click on 'Renew' → dispatch('handleRenew') → chain.invoke('renew',[name]) immediately; renewal costs the same getPrice(length) (2 GAS for 5+ chars) but no cost is displayed anywhere and there is no confirm step — violates the cluster's fee-transparency bar.

medium_low.evidence: ownerOf returns 20 raw bytes; parseByteLike falls through to '0x'+hex of the little-endian buffer, so the UI shows e.g. 0xfda64993… which matches neither explorer (big-endian) nor wallet (N-address) formats.

medium_low.title: Docs config strands most of the written guide; dead legacy files

Also src/pages/index/neo-ns-theme.scss (old green-terminal theme) and src/utils/neoHelpers.ts (duplicate domainToTokenId/ensureNeoWalletAndChain) are referenced by nothing.

purpose: Pick one die face, stake GAS, and have Morpheus VRF settle a 5.70x payout on Neo N3 (mainnet/testnet) or Neo X mainnet.

journeys.name: Place bet on Neo N3 (deposit + placeDiceBet)
journeys.detail: UI form → dispatch placeDiceBet → invokeWithPayment (GAS transfer memo 'miniapp-dice-game:stake', waitForDepositConfirmation, then placeDiceBet(appId,player,chosenNumber,amount) — args/events verified against PlatformGame ABI). The shared flow correctly confirms the deposit before the consuming call. BUT the contract asserts house liquidity >= stake*5.7 only inside placeDiceBet, i.e. AFTER the deposit tx already landed; verified via RPC the mainnet contract (0xa7840a8d) holds 1.45 GAS, so any stake above ~0.25 GAS — including the UI's own 0.50/1.00/5.00 presets — fails post-deposit and strands the stake as credit. PlatformGame exposes no withdraw method (verified on-chain), so the only exit is a future successful small bet.

journeys.name: Place bet on Neo X (EVM, atomic)
journeys.detail: ensureEvmWallet → invokeEvmWithValue placeBet(uint8) with stake as msg.value (atomic — a revert returns funds), requestId from BetPlaced topic, then getBet(requestId) polled 45×4s until VRF status > Pending. Status enum mapping (2=won/3=lost/4=refunded) is clean. Testnet Neo X correctly rejected with a clear (but untranslated) error.

journeys.name: Watch settlement + roll history
journeys.detail: Per-bet tracker (bet-tracker.ts) settles each bet into its own row by id and pins the banner/dice to the active bet — interleaved bets cannot stomp each other; win fires fireworks via success status. Friction: history is session-local (cap 6); a reload during the up-to-3-minute resolve loop loses the pending bet entirely with no chain hydration, even though DiceBetPlaced/Resolved events are listable per app; a poll timeout leaves the row 'Rolling…' forever with no retry affordance.

journeys.name: Recover stranded stake credit
journeys.detail: After a post-deposit failure the UI says 'Your GAS is locked and refundable via the contract', but the deployed PlatformGame has no withdraw/refund-credit method (RPC-verified) and the app never reads or displays getDirectGasCredit. The honest path — credit auto-funds the next roll — is neither shown nor explained.

journeys.name: Fund stake via host operation panel
journeys.detail: neo-manifest.json operation_panel exposes 'Fund Stake' → method fundGameCredit, but main.tsx never registers that action; MiniAppRoot.handleAction only console.warns on a missing handler, so the host-side button silently does nothing.

confirmed_high.title: Mainnet house liquidity (1.45 GAS) makes the app's own stake presets strand funds
confirmed_high.evidence: PlatformGame.Dice.cs:84-85 asserts GAS.BalanceOf(contract) >= amount*6*95/100 inside placeDiceBet — i.e. after invokeWithPayment's deposit tx has already landed and been credited. RPC: contract 0xa7840a8d holds 1.4479 GAS on mainnet, so max safe stake ≈ 0.25 GAS, yet PlayArea presets are 0.10/0.50/1.00/5.00 and max input is 20 GAS. Any preset ≥ 0.50 deposits first, then faults 'insufficient payout liquidity', stranding the GAS as non-withdrawable credit.
confirmed_high.fix: Before the deposit step, read GAS balanceOf(contract) (or extend getDiceBetLimits) and refuse/clamp the stake with an explicit 'house can currently pay up to X GAS' message; surface the live house liquidity next to the Odds/Fee/Range metrics; ops-side, fund the mainnet contract.

confirmed_high.title: 'Refundable via the contract' recovery message is false; credit is invisible
confirmed_high.evidence: statusFundsRecoverable: 'Your GAS is locked and refundable via the contract' — but the deployed PlatformGame ABI (RPC-verified) has no withdraw/refund-credit method; only DiceBetRefunded for placed-but-unsettleable bets. getDirectGasCredit exists but the app never reads it, so the user can't even see the stranded amount.
confirmed_high.fix: Read getDirectGasCredit(appId, player) in loadData and after failures; show a 'You have X GAS credit — it will fund your next roll automatically' banner; reword statusFundsRecoverable accordingly (en+zh).

medium_low.title: Host operation panel 'Fund Stake' dispatches an unregistered action (silent no-op)
medium_low.evidence: operation_panel operation 'Fund Stake' → method 'fundGameCredit'; main.tsx registers only placeDiceBet. MiniAppRoot.tsx:409 handles a missing handler with console.warn and returns — the user gets zero feedback.
medium_low.fix: Register a fundGameCredit action (GAS transfer with the 'miniapp-dice-game:stake' memo only) or remove the operation from neo-manifest.json so the host never renders the dead button.

medium_low.title: Pending bets and history vanish on reload — no chain hydration
medium_low.evidence: loadData only calls refreshNetwork(); rollHistory lives purely in the tracker observables. A refresh during the 3-minute resolveN3Bet poll discards the bet — the payout still lands on-chain but the app shows 'No local roll history yet.'
medium_low.fix: In loadData, hydrate the last N DiceBetPlaced/DiceBetResolved events (already filterable by app via listEvents) matched to the connected player into rollHistory, and resume polling for any unresolved betId.

medium_low.title: Hardcoded English error for unsupported Neo X testnet
medium_low.evidence: throw new Error("Neo X dice is live on mainnet only. Switch to Neo X Mainnet or use Neo N3 for testnet play.") — surfaces untranslated in the status bar and form error in zh locale.
medium_low.fix: Add an en+zh locale key (e.g. neoXMainnetOnly) and throw ctx.t('neoXMainnetOnly').

medium_low.title: Stake silently clamped at submit when network cap changed since page load
medium_low.evidence: placeDiceBet refreshes the network then sanitizeAmount clamps the typed amount to the new maxStake (e.g. 10 GAS typed on N3 becomes a 2 GAS bet after switching the wallet to Neo X) without telling the user; amounts <0.05 are silently raised to 0.05.
medium_low.fix: If the sanitized amount differs from the submitted one, abort with a clear 'stake exceeds the X GAS cap on <network>' error instead of betting a different amount.

medium_low.title: Limits hardcoded instead of read from getDiceBetLimits
medium_low.evidence: maxStakeOf returns hardcoded 2/20 and MIN_STAKE=0.05 in PlayArea, while the contract exposes getDiceBetLimits(appId) — UI drifts if the contract config changes.
medium_low.fix: Fetch getDiceBetLimits in refreshNetwork (N3 path) and bind min/max/presets to it, keeping the hardcoded values as fallback.

purpose: Heads-or-tails GAS coin flip with instant on-chain settlement and 2x payout from a house bankroll (MiniAppCoinFlip).

journeys.name: Place a flip with existing credit
journeys.detail: choice/amount validated → flip(player, choice 0|1, amountBase) → Flipped event slots [3]=outcome [4]=won [5]=payout (verified against MiniAppCoinFlip ABI, deployed at 0x5d82339d on both nets) → win overlay or loss flash → loadAll() reconciles stats + history from getStats/getPlayerGames. Base-unit math via gasToBaseUnits, no floats.

journeys.name: Place a flip that needs a deposit (first bet)
journeys.detail: When creditOf < wager the composable broadcasts a raw GAS transfer (memo 'miniapp-fogplay:bet') and IMMEDIATELY invokes flip with no waitForDepositConfirmation — the flip's test-invoke runs against pre-deposit state and faults 'insufficient credit', so the user sees the scary 'Wager prepaid but the flip didn't settle' error and must press Flip again (second attempt succeeds off the now-settled credit). The shared helper exists precisely for this (useContractInteraction.ts:80-86 'Exported so per-app composables… adopt the same settle-before-consume pattern').

journeys.name: Bet larger than the house bankroll
journeys.detail: Bankroll is only read AFTER flip fails; the deposit has already landed. RPC: mainnet bankroll() = 2 GAS while MAX_BET=100 and presets are 1/5/10/50 GAS — a 50 GAS preset deposits 50 GAS, then flip reverts 'bankroll cannot cover', leaving 50 GAS as credit the UI offers no way to withdraw.

journeys.name: Withdraw stranded bet credit
journeys.detail: The deployed contract HAS withdraw(account) + CreditWithdrawn (RPC-verified on both nets) and the locale even ships a depositStranded message telling users to 'withdraw from your balance' — but no UI control calls withdraw and creditOf is never displayed. Money-in without money-out.

journeys.name: Pick heads/tails
journeys.detail: dispatch('setChoice') updates the observable and placeBet bets the right side, but PlayArea reads choice via useMemo(() => state.choice?.get(), [state]) with a stable state identity — the memo never recomputes, so the highlighted card and aria-pressed stay on 'heads' forever even when the user is actually betting tails.

journeys.name: View stats and game history
journeys.detail: wins/losses/totalWon from getStats; history pages in the newest 20 game ids via playerGameCount + getPlayerGames(offset) then getGame each — survives reloads, newest first, payout column correct.

confirmed_high.title: Choice selector frozen by useMemo([state]) — UI shows 'heads' while betting tails
confirmed_high.evidence: const choice = useMemo(() => (state.choice?.get() ?? "heads"), [state]); — the state record identity never changes across renders (appStateRef.current in MiniAppRoot), so the memo returns the first-render value forever. WagerControls highlights and aria-presses the stale side; placeBet uses the real observable, so the bet diverges from the visual selection.
confirmed_high.fix: Use the live accessor like every other binding: const choice = str("choice", "heads") as "heads"|"tails"; (useStateBindings already re-renders on the observable change).

confirmed_high.title: Deposit→flip race: no deposit confirmation before the consuming call
confirmed_high.evidence: placeBet broadcasts chain.invoke('transfer', …, GAS_HASH) then immediately chain.invoke('flip', …). useContractInteraction.ts:80-86 documents that deposit-then-act contracts fault when the consuming call lands first and exports waitForDepositConfirmation for exactly this; ChainService.prepayAndInvoke (ChainService.ts:552) already implements the confirmed pattern. Every first/funded bet fails once with 'betPrepaidNoFlip' and requires a second click.
confirmed_high.fix: Replace the two raw invokes with chain.prepayAndInvoke(amountBase, BET_MEMO, 'flip', args, { waitForEvent: 'Flipped' }), or insert await waitForDepositConfirmation(transferTxid, { network }) between the steps.

confirmed_high.title: No pre-flight bankroll check — large presets strand GAS as credit (mainnet bankroll is 2 GAS)
confirmed_high.evidence: bankroll() is only consulted in the error handler after flip reverts; the deposit has already settled. RPC: mainnet bankroll = 200000000 (2 GAS) while BET_PRESETS go to 50 GAS and MAX_BET=100 — the 5/10/50 presets all deposit first then fail, locking the wager as credit with no withdraw UI.
confirmed_high.fix: Read bankroll() in loadAll and before depositing; disable/grey presets above the payable cap, show 'max payable bet: X GAS' near the wager input, and refuse the deposit when wager > bankroll.

medium_low.title: withdraw(account) exists on-chain but the app has no withdraw-credit UI and never shows creditOf
medium_low.evidence: creditOf(player) is read only as an internal top-up check; the contract's withdraw(account)/CreditWithdrawn (verified on 0x5d82339d both nets) is never called, and the shipped depositStranded message ('withdraw from your balance to recover the GAS') is unused dead copy.
medium_low.fix: Surface a credit chip ('Prepaid credit: X GAS') with a Withdraw button dispatching invoke('withdraw', [player]) and reload; reuse the existing depositStranded/betPrepaidNoFlip strings.

medium_low.title: Copy claims oracle randomness but settlement is on-chain GetRandom
medium_low.evidence: docSubtitle 'Oracle-backed coin toss', docDescription 'requests randomness through the Morpheus Oracle flow', step3 'wait for the oracle callback', feature1 'Oracle Callback' — but the contract settles atomically with Runtime.GetRandom in the same tx (useCoinFlip.ts header documents this). Misstates the trust model and tells users to wait for a callback that never happens.
medium_low.fix: Rewrite docSubtitle/docDescription/step3/feature1 (en+zh) plus manifest.ts:23 description to 'instant on-chain settlement via Neo's native randomness, paid in the same transaction'.

medium_low.title: Missing 'eyebrow' locale key → hardcoded English 'ORACLE COIN TOSS' in zh
medium_low.evidence: t("eyebrow") || "ORACLE COIN TOSS" — the key is absent from messages.ts; useI18n returns "" in prod (the literal key in dev), so zh users see English (and the fallback repeats the wrong oracle claim).
medium_low.fix: Add eyebrow: { en: 'On-chain coin toss', zh: '链上抛硬币' } to messages.ts and drop the hardcoded fallback.

medium_low.title: Two unexplained wallet prompts per funded bet
medium_low.evidence: A first-time bet signs a deposit transfer then a flip with no UI hint that two confirmations are expected; users may reject the second prompt thinking it's a duplicate.
medium_low.fix: Show a small 'step 1/2: fund wager → step 2/2: flip' hint while isFlipping during the deposit leg (state already distinguishes the phases once prepayAndInvoke is adopted).

purpose: Gacha market: creators publish weighted prize machines (GAS/NEO escrowed on-chain), players pay GAS to pull and win real on-chain prizes (MiniAppGasBox).

journeys.name: Browse and select a machine
journeys.detail: loadMachines enumerates ids 1..lastMachineId via getMachine + per-item getItem (caps 500/100), derives rarity from weight share, pool-readiness from poolBalance >= maxPrize, and a readiness checklist before pulling — excellent transparency. Friction: mainnet (the default network) currently has ZERO machines (RPC: lastMachineId=0), so first impression is the empty state; per-machine reads are an N+1 RPC fan-out.

journeys.name: Pull a machine
journeys.detail: playCreditOf checked, top-up transfer (memo 'miniapp-gasbox:play') broadcast, then pull(machineId, player) invoked IMMEDIATELY with no deposit confirmation — same race as fogplay: the funded first pull faults at test-invoke and must be retried; on retry the credit covers it and the Pulled event (slots [3]=itemIndex [4]=prizeAmount, ABI-verified) drives a correct prize overlay with the on-chain amount.

journeys.name: Publish a machine (Studio)
journeys.detail: createMachine → MachineCreated id (with sensible fallbacks) → addItem ×N → pool funding transfer (memo 'miniapp-gasbox-pool:<id>') → setActive, each waiting for its event. Correct per the ABI, weight-derived tier preview matches read-back. Friction: 3+N sequential wallet signatures with no step-progress indicator; a rejection mid-flow leaves an inactive machine (items partial, pool possibly funded) with no resume path.

journeys.name: Withdraw creator revenue
journeys.detail: Withdraw Revenue shown only when the connected wallet matches creatorHash and revenueRaw > 0; withdrawRevenue(creator, machineId, to) matches the ABI; machines reload after.

journeys.name: Top up / reactivate a drained machine
journeys.detail: Once prizes drain the pool below maxPrize the machine blocks ('Inventory needs funding before players can pull') and the copy points to Studio — but Studio only creates NEW machines; there is no UI to send the pool memo transfer or call setActive on an existing machine, although the contract supports both. Machines die permanently from the UI's perspective.

journeys.name: Recover pool funds / withdraw play credit
journeys.detail: The contract has NO pool-withdraw and NO play-credit-withdraw method (ABI-verified): escrowed pool funds exit only as prizes, and stranded play credit only via a future pull. Neither limitation is disclosed before the creator deposits maxPrize, and playCreditOf is never displayed to players.

confirmed_high.title: Deposit→pull race: prepay transfer not confirmed before pull
confirmed_high.evidence: When playCreditOf < price the composable broadcasts chain.invoke('transfer', …, GAS_HASH) and immediately chain.invoke('pull', …, { waitForEvent: 'Pulled' }) — no waitForDepositConfirmation, despite the shared helper being exported for exactly this pattern (useContractInteraction.ts:80-86) and prepayAndInvoke existing on ChainService. Every credit-funded first pull errors once and must be retried.
confirmed_high.fix: Use chain.prepayAndInvoke(priceBase.toString(), PLAY_MEMO, 'pull', args, { waitForEvent: 'Pulled' }), or await waitForDepositConfirmation(transferTxid, { network }) between the transfer and the pull.

confirmed_high.title: Drained machines cannot be re-funded or re-activated from the UI; blocked-state copy points to a dead end
confirmed_high.evidence: gasboxPullBlockedInventory says 'fund prizes in Studio' and gasboxPullBlockedInactive says 'open Studio to update it', but the Studio renders only the create-new-machine form. The contract fully supports topping up (transfer with memo 'miniapp-gasbox-pool:<id>') and setActive(creator, machineId, true/false), so a machine whose pool drops below maxPrize is permanently dead from the UI even for its creator.
confirmed_high.fix: On the selected-machine card, when the connected wallet is the creator, add 'Top up pool' (amount input → pool-memo transfer → reload) and an Activate/Deactivate toggle (setActive), and reword the blocked-state copy to point at them.

medium_low.title: Studio collects description/category/tags that are silently discarded
medium_low.evidence: createMachine(creator, name, prizeAsset, price) stores none of these (ABI-verified); publishMachine never sends them and readMachine hardcodes description/category/tags to "" (useGasBox.ts:326-330), so the card UI that renders machine.description can never show anything. Users type metadata that vanishes after publish.
medium_low.fix: Remove the three dead fields from the Studio form (and the conditional renders), or persist them via ctx.os.storage keyed by machineId and merge them into readMachine results.

medium_low.title: Multi-signature publish has no step progress and no resume after mid-flow failure
medium_low.evidence: Publishing signs 3+N transactions (create, N×addItem, fund, activate) behind a single 'Publishing…' spinner; if the user rejects signature 3 of 6, a half-built inactive machine remains on-chain with no UI to add the missing items, fund, or activate it later (only the generic poolCannotCoverMaxPrize error on the activation step is handled).
medium_low.fix: Show 'step k of N' status via the existing setStatus callback during publish, and in the market list flag the creator's own inactive machines with a 'Resume setup' affordance (add items / fund pool / activate) reusing the same calls.

medium_low.title: Irreversibility of pool escrow not disclosed before deposit
medium_low.evidence: inventoryNote explains that publishing funds the pool but not that MiniAppGasBox has no pool-withdraw method (ABI-verified) — escrowed funds can only ever leave as player prizes; deactivating locks them forever. Creators commit maxPrize without knowing it is one-way.
medium_low.fix: Append an explicit en+zh warning to inventoryNote: 'Pool deposits are non-recoverable — they pay out only as prizes', and repeat it next to the publish button.

medium_low.title: Machine cards always show '0 plays'
medium_low.evidence: readMachine hardcodes plays: 0 (useGasBox.ts:340) while main.tsx already derives est. plays as floor(revenue/price) for the global stat — every card misleadingly reads '0 plays' regardless of volume.
medium_low.fix: Compute the same floor(revenueRaw/priceRaw) per machine in readMachine and label it 'est. plays' (matching estPlaysHint), or drop the plays meta from cards.

medium_low.title: Player play-credit is invisible (reuse-only, no display)
medium_low.evidence: playCreditOf is read internally to skip the deposit but never surfaced; after a stranded prepay (race failure / abandoned pull) the next pull silently consumes the credit and the user is never told funds were waiting — nor that the contract has no credit-withdraw method.
medium_low.fix: Expose playCredit as state and render a 'Prepaid credit: X GAS — your next pull uses it automatically' chip near the pull button when > 0.

medium_low.title: Mainnet market is empty on the default network
medium_low.evidence: default_network is neo-n3-mainnet but RPC shows lastMachineId() = 0 there (testnet has 1) — every mainnet first-run lands on the empty state. The empty state itself is good (refresh + open studio CTAs).
medium_low.fix: Seed one or two house machines on mainnet (small GAS prizes), or have the empty state explicitly invite creators with the expected cost (maxPrize escrow) so the cold-start is intentional.

purpose: Claim a server-backed 1-50 GAS random reward via a OneGate QR single-use key; creators can also run on-chain range-reward GAS pools (create/top-up/refund).

journeys.name: Claim via OneGate QR key (claim-only launch)
journeys.detail: Launch param claimKey → claim-only screen → resolveClaimAddress (OneGate injected address with diagnostics, wallet fallback) → POST /api/onegate-vault/claim → 4-step progress (wallet/submitting/confirming/paid) with status polling → receipt with amount, masked key, luck %, txid. Backend infra is live again. Polished flow with aria-live, error+diagnostics split.

journeys.name: Check claim status
journeys.detail: checkClaimStatus → GET /api/onegate-vault/status with identity params, updates claimStatus/progress/lastClaimAmount. Reachable from the host operations panel (claimPool with claimKey) and re-runs cleanly.

journeys.name: Create an on-chain range pool
journeys.detail: createPool validates (1 GAS min, 1-50 range, 1-100 slots, ≤720h) then invokeWithPayment(createRangeGasPool…) — but RPC getcontractstate shows BOTH wired hashes (mainnet 0x5f371cc5, testnet 0xfa1b7240) are MiniAppRedEnvelope deployments with NO Range* methods; the deposit memo 'gas-lucky-pool:create:N' also fails RedEnvelope's memo assert, so the wallet test-invoke faults and nothing can be created. Even with correct wiring, the expiry argument is sent in SECONDS where the contract expects MILLISECONDS, so a 24h pool would expire in 86 seconds.

journeys.name: Inspect / top-up / refund a pool, withdraw gas credit
journeys.detail: All five controls exist (good exits on paper, including withdrawGasCredit) but target the same wrong RedEnvelope contract → every call faults. Additionally 'Inspect Pool' is a UI dead-end even when it succeeds: loadPool stores currentPool and loadAll fills recentPools/recentClaims, but PlayArea never renders any of them — the button produces zero visible output.

journeys.name: Distribute a pool to claimers (share link/QR)
journeys.detail: currentShareUrl is derived in the composable but never rendered anywhere, and buildLegacyPoolClaimUrl produces a '?pool=<id>' link with no claimKey — recipients opening it land on the CREATOR workspace (the claim screen requires launchClaimKey) and the host operations panel marks claimKey required, so there is no path for a recipient to claim a range pool.

journeys.name: Claim via host operation panel 'Claim Reward' (claimOneGateVault)
journeys.detail: neo-manifest.json operation_panel declares method claimOneGateVault but main.tsx registers only claimPool/checkClaimStatus/etc. — MiniAppRoot.handleAction console.warns and silently no-ops. (The in-app src/manifest.ts operations correctly use claimPool, so only the host-manifest panel is dead.)

confirmed_high.title: On-chain pool suite is wired to the wrong contract (MiniAppRedEnvelope) on BOTH networks
confirmed_high.evidence: RPC getcontractstate: mainnet 0x5f371cc50116bb13d79554d96ccdd6e246cd5d59 and testnet 0xfa1b7240fead2a63999c02defa3aec5eb274a919 both resolve to name 'MiniAppRedEnvelope' with zero Range*/withdrawGasCredit methods, while the app invokes createRangeGasPool/claimRangeGasPool/fundRangeGasPool/refundRangeGasPool/getDirectGasCredit/withdrawGasCredit (PlatformSocial ABI). apps/shared/constants/generated-miniapp-contracts.ts:23,64 carries the same wrong hashes. Every on-chain action faults; the create deposit memo also fails RedEnvelope's 'invalid memo' assert.
confirmed_high.fix: Deploy (or locate) the PlatformSocial build that contains the RangePool module, update neo-manifest.json contracts + the generated registry to its hashes, and add a deploy-script live-validation harness; until then hide the creator workspace behind a 'temporarily unavailable' notice instead of letting every button fail.

confirmed_high.title: Expiry sent in seconds but contract expects milliseconds — pools would die ~1000× early
confirmed_high.evidence: validateCreateForm returns expirySeconds = Math.round(expiryHours * 3600) and createPool passes it as the expiry arg (line 314), but PlatformSocial.Envelope.RangePool.cs:32-33 states 'expiryMs is the lifetime in milliseconds (Runtime.Time is ms)' — a 24-hour pool would be claimable for 86 seconds. The UI status check has the mirror bug: parsePool (useGasLuckyPool.shared.ts:101) compares Date.now()/1000 (seconds) against the on-chain ms ExpiryTime, so expired pools would render as 'active'.
confirmed_high.fix: Send expiryHours * 3600 * 1000 to createRangeGasPool and compare Date.now() (ms) > expiryTime in parsePool; add a unit test pinning the ms convention.

confirmed_high.title: 'Inspect Pool' loads data the UI never renders — pool details, recent pools and claims are invisible
confirmed_high.evidence: PlayArea destructures none of currentPool, recentPools, recentClaims, currentShareUrl, currentRange, totalRemaining despite all being exposed in state (main.tsx:230-263); after Inspect Pool succeeds the only feedback is the absence of an error toast. A creator can never see remaining amount, claimed count, expiry or status of their pool.
