journeys.detail: The Request card stays fully enabled (quota 0.1 from the fallback), the user picks an amount and clicks Request GAS -> requestSponsorship throws MiniAppError 'Platform API not configured' (PLATFORM_API empty) or 'Sponsorship request failed' (live API 503). Developer-facing error toast; no degraded-state messaging anywhere.

journeys.name: donate GAS to the pool
journeys.detail: Donation itself is a plain GAS transfer to a hardcoded pool address and would work on-chain — but the entire Pay-It-Forward card is locked behind isFunded, which derives from the API's silently-zeroed gas_balance. With the API degraded/unconfigured, every wallet sees 'Get funded first', so a working feature is unreachable for everyone.

journeys.name: send GAS to a friend
journeys.detail: Same isFunded gate as donate; the address validation (base58, 34 chars, N prefix) and chain transfer are sound (the host WIF adapter converts address->script hash for Hash160 args, verified in platform/host-app/lib/wallet/adapters/wif.ts:285), but the form can never be reached while the API reports zero balance.

journeys.name: view on-chain sponsor pool stats (implied by the deployed contract)
journeys.detail: The manifest declares MiniAppGasSponsor (mainnet 0x80ea8435, verified live with getPoolData/getTotalSponsored/getSponsorStats/getBeneficiaryStats/whitelist methods) but no code in the app ever reads it; the 'Stats' tab in the manifest shows nothing on-chain.

medium_low.title: Manifest tabs (Sponsor/Donate/Send/Stats) do not switch anything
medium_low.evidence: Lines 17-22 declare four tabs, but PlayArea.tsx never reads the active tab — all four render the identical single-scroll page, so tapping Donate/Send/Stats appears to do nothing.
medium_low.fix: Drop the extra tabs (keep the single 'sponsor' tab like neo-pay does) or read the active tab from props and scroll/show the matching section.

medium_low.title: Donations bypass the deployed sponsor contract and its on-chain pool accounting
medium_low.evidence: handleDonate (175-184) transfers GAS to the hardcoded EOA SPONSOR_POOL_ADDRESS 'NhWxcoEc9qtmnjsTLF1fVF6myJ5MZZhSMK' (line 20), while neo-manifest.json:24-25 declares MiniAppGasSponsor 0x80ea8435 whose live ABI (verified) tracks pools, sponsors, badges (getPoolData/getTotalSponsored/hasSponsorBadge). Donors get no on-chain credit and the pool totals stay invisible.
medium_low.fix: Route donations to the contract's pool flow (or at minimum read getTotalSponsored/getPoolCount for an honest on-chain stats section), and move the pool address into config rather than a hardcoded constant.

medium_low.title: resetTime placeholder check breaks under zh locale
medium_low.evidence: Line 117 renders an em-dash only when resetTime !== 'N/A', but the composable returns t('notAvailable') (useGasSponsor.ts:64) which is '不可用' in zh (shared base-messages.ts:27), so zh users see the literal '不可用' instead of '—'.
medium_low.fix: Have resetTime return '' when resetsAt is empty and let the UI default to '—' — never compare against a translated string.

medium_low.title: Donate field shows an error before the user touches it
medium_low.evidence: donateTouched (line 51) treats the pre-filled default '0.1' as touched, so a funded wallet holding under 0.1 GAS opens the card with 'Enter an amount up to your balance' already displayed — contradicting the code comment 'forms don't open in an error state'.
medium_low.fix: Track touched state from the input's onChange (a local useState flag) instead of inferring it from the default value.

purpose: Execute instant uncollateralized GAS loans repaid in the same transaction via a user-supplied onFlashLoan callback contract, with on-chain loan lookup and pool stats.

journeys.name: request flash loan
journeys.detail: The app invokes 'requestFlashLoan(appId, borrower, amount, callbackContract, method)' but the deployed MiniAppFlashLoan on BOTH networks exposes requestLoan(borrower, amount, callbackContract, callbackMethod) — no appId, different name. Verified live via getcontractstate on mainnet 0xb5d8fb0d and testnet 0xde8e595d. The wallet invoke faults with 'method not found'. Even after fixing the name, the mainnet pool balance is 0 (live getPlatformStats read), so no loan can execute.

journeys.name: lookup loan status
journeys.detail: Reads 'getFlashLoan(appId, loanId)'; the contract has getLoan(loanId) / getLoanDetails(loanId). The read faults and, because the lookupLoan action is dispatched without notify.guard, the raw VM exception ('System.Contract.Call failed: method not found...') bubbles into the toast.

journeys.name: view pool stats and recent executions
journeys.detail: Reads 'getFlashLoanStats(appId)' — confirmed FAULT live ('method not found: getFlashLoanStats/1'). The catch silently zeroes everything, so the hero permanently shows 0 pool / 0 loans / 0 fees with hardcoded default limits, indistinguishable from a healthy empty pool. The correct method getPlatformStats() exists and returns exactly the fields the parser expects (totalLoans/totalBorrowed/totalFees/poolBalance/minLoan/maxLoan/feeBasisPoints — verified live, fee 9bps, max 100k GAS).

journeys.name: provide liquidity / earn fees (implied by the contract's business model)
journeys.detail: The deployed contract has deposit/withdraw/distributeFees, provider stats, provider badges and an 80% providerFeeShare — a full LP product — but the UI exposes none of it. Since the pool can only be funded through this missing flow, the entire lending side is a dead end on mainnet (pool = 0).

journeys.name: prepare an onFlashLoan callback contract (prerequisite)
journeys.detail: Every loan requires a deployed callback contract implementing onFlashLoan; the UI just asks for '0x...' with no sample contract, template, or documentation link, making the journey impossible for anyone who is not already a Neo contract developer.

medium_low.title: Read failures silently zero the hero stats with no user-visible notice
medium_low.evidence: loadLoanStats catch (lines 264-270) console.warns and sets stats/pool/recentLoans to zeros and defaults — currently every load takes this path, and the UI presents fabricated '0.0000 Pool Balance / 0 Loans' as fact.
medium_low.fix: Add a serviceNotice observable set in the catch, render a warning banner in PlayArea (pattern: neo-pay's neopay-service-notice), and keep the last good snapshot instead of zeroing.

medium_low.title: lookupLoan dispatch is unguarded — raw VM exceptions reach the toast
medium_low.evidence: Lines 53-57: ctx.registerAction('lookupLoan', ...) awaits flash.lookupLoan(id) directly with no notify.guard, unlike the other actions; a faulting read surfaces 'System.Contract.Call failed: method not found: getFlashLoan/2' verbatim via the kernel's default error toast.
medium_low.fix: Wrap in notify.guard(() => flash.lookupLoan(id), undefined, 'loanNotFound') and map read FAULTs to the existing loanNotFound/notAvailable messages.

medium_low.title: Callback-contract prerequisite is unexplained; loan constraints never shown pre-flight
medium_low.evidence: The form (lines 253-262) asks for 'Callback Contract 0x...' with only a fixed 'onFlashLoan' method label; no sample contract, interface snippet, or docs link. Cooldown (5 min) and max-daily-loans (10) limits exist on-chain (live getPlatformStats: loanCooldownSeconds=300, maxDailyLoans=10) and in contractStats, but are never rendered, so a second request inside the cooldown fails opaquely. Note the parser also reads the wrong field name (cooldownMs vs loanCooldownSeconds, useFlashloanCore.ts:231).
medium_low.fix: Render cooldown/daily-limit rows in the Loan Calculator card, fix the field mapping (loanCooldownSeconds*1000), and link a minimal onFlashLoan example contract in the hero or docs section.

medium_low.title: Post-request refresh reads stale state — no event wait on the loan invoke
medium_low.evidence: requestLoan invoke (332-341) passes no waitForEvent, then loadData() (357) runs immediately after broadcast, so stats/history reads (also 30s-cached, lines 215-217 cache:true) predate the loan's execution and the new loan never appears without a manual reload.
medium_low.fix: Pass { waitForEvent: 'LoanExecuted' } (event exists in the deployed ABI) on the invoke and bypass the read cache on the post-action refresh.

purpose: NEO <-> GAS conversion with live price-feed quotes, slippage context and (per the UI) one-click on-chain swap execution.

journeys.name: view live quote / refresh rate
journeys.detail: useMorpheusDataFeed reads getLatest on the mainnet MorpheusDataFeed 0x03013f49 directly over RPC. Verified live: NEO-USD 2.182 and GAS-USD 1.101 with data timestamps under an hour old — the feed really is updating again, so the quote journey is healthy. Refresh button re-derives the cross rate (~1.98 GAS/NEO).

journeys.name: preview conversion + min received
journeys.detail: Strict decimal parsing (rejects fractional NEO with a clear 'NEO is indivisible' message), output = amount * rate, min received = 0.995x with the fixed 0.5% slippage display. Derived values bind to the right observables; toAmount recomputes on amount/rate/pair changes without reload.

journeys.name: switch pair / select token
journeys.detail: Selector modal, direction flip, and PopularPairs all dispatch correctly and reload the rate; balances come from the chain BalanceService and refresh after actions.

journeys.name: execute swap
journeys.detail: neo-manifest.json declares NO contracts ('contracts': {}) and only read:blockchain permission, yet the UI shows an enabled primary 'Swap NEO -> GAS' button once rate+balance pass (canSwap never checks for a router) and a 'Route ready' badge fabricated from mere rate presence. Clicking walks the user through wallet connect and then throws 'Swap router unavailable' (useSwapEngine.ts:220-221). The swapTokenInForTokenOut router call is unreachable by construction — the core promise of the screen cannot complete.

medium_low.title: No feed-staleness guard on quotes
medium_low.evidence: loadExchangeRate (148-167) uses datafeed.getPrice which discards the on-chain dataTimestamp the feed stores (this very feed froze for ~3 months earlier this year; live reads today show GAS updated 26 min before NEO). A stale price would quote silently with no 'as of' context.
medium_low.fix: Extend useMorpheusDataFeed.getPrice to return {price, dataTimestamp}, display 'as of HH:MM' next to the rate, and flip the route badge to a warning when the older leg exceeds ~15 minutes.

medium_low.title: Manifest 'Route' tab renders identical content
medium_low.evidence: Lines 19-22 declare swap + pool tabs but PlayArea never reads the active tab; 'Route Liquidity'/'Route Depth'/'Your Preview' locale keys (messages.ts:15,55-57) are orphaned. Tapping 'Route' does nothing visible.
medium_low.fix: Remove the pool tab (single-tab pattern like neo-pay) or render an actual route/liquidity panel under it.

medium_low.title: Tiny min-received values collapse to zero slippage protection
medium_low.evidence: Line 218-219: minOutputAmount.toString() emits scientific notation below 1e-7 ('9.95e-8'), which toFixedDecimals rejects to '0' (apps/shared/utils/format.ts:75-88) — the swap would then accept any output. Latent until a router exists, but the math path is wrong today.
medium_low.fix: Compute minOutput in integer base units: minOutputInt = amountInt * rate-derived bigint * 995n / 1000n, never via float .toString().

medium_low.title: selectPair fallback status and stale sample rate are untranslated/dead copy
medium_low.evidence: Line 59 uses ctx.t('pairUnavailable') but no such key exists in locale/messages.ts, so zh falls back to inline English 'Pair x unavailable'; messages.ts:101 still ships hardcoded 'neoGasRate: 1 NEO ≈ 8.5 GAS' (4x off today's live 1.98) — unused dead copy that risks being wired up.
medium_low.fix: Add pairUnavailable {en,zh} to messages.ts and delete the neoGasRate key.

medium_low.title: MAX on GAS leaves no fee headroom; token monograms instead of shipped icons
medium_low.evidence: setMaxAmount (138-141) sets the full GAS balance, which cannot settle once network fees apply; meanwhile src/static/neo-token.png and gas-token.png ship in the bundle but the selector and hero render single-letter initials (PlayArea.tsx:117,158,255).
medium_low.fix: Reserve ~0.1 GAS in setMaxAmount when fromToken is GAS, and swap the letter monograms for the bundled token images.

purpose: Track public Neo Foundation founder-wallet balances (with USD totals from the on-chain price feed) and submit controlled NEO/GAS disbursements from the connected wallet.

journeys.name: View foundation treasury balances on load
journeys.detail: loadData runs on mount via lifecycle.onDataLoad: cache-first paint, then 44 addresses fetched in bounded-concurrency chunks of 8 with per-wallet failure isolation; USD totals from shared getPrices() reading mainnet MorpheusDataFeed 0x03013f49 — verified live (NEO=$2.177, updated 2026-06-11 23:55 UTC), so the formerly-stale USD figures are now fresh.

journeys.name: Drill into per-wallet balances per founder group
journeys.detail: Each group card lists all wallets with label, compact address, NEO/GAS figures in a scrollable 248px list; hover states present.

journeys.name: Refresh treasury data
journeys.detail: Refresh button dispatches the refresh action → loadData; button disabled and relabeled while refreshing; failure with cache present falls back silently to cache (see stale-cache finding).

journeys.name: Connect wallet
journeys.detail: connectWallet action calls chain.ensureWallet(), syncs address observable, button flips to 'Wallet connected'; address changes from the host are also synced via chain.address.subscribe (main.tsx:141).

journeys.name: Submit NEO/GAS disbursement
journeys.detail: Form → buildTreasuryDisbursementPreview live-validates (BigInt base-unit scaling, NEO whole-token rule, GAS 8-dec rule, Hash160/address normalization) with an auto-opening signing-intent panel showing native contract, fixed8 amount, recipient Hash160, signer; submit → chain.invoke('transfer', args, {scriptHash}) against the native NEO/GAS contract (valid InvokeOptions per ChainService.ts:383); txid receipt rendered, success toast only on success path.

journeys.name: See disbursement reflected in watched balances
journeys.detail: After a successful transfer there is no automatic loadData() — if the recipient is one of the 44 watched wallets the dashboard stays stale until the user manually presses Refresh.

medium_low.title: Stale cached data displayed as 'Live balances synced' when fresh fetch fails
medium_low.evidence: loadData sets data from readCachedJSON first; if fetchTreasuryData() then throws and cache exists, the error is only console.warn'd. PlayArea computes hasLiveData=Boolean(data) and shows the green dot + t('treasuryLiveSynced') — so day-old cached figures render as freshly synced.
medium_low.fix: Add a `stale` observable set true when the fresh fetch fails but cache exists; render an amber dot + 'Showing cached data from {lastUpdated}' signal instead of treasuryLiveSynced.

medium_low.title: Partial RPC failures silently zero wallet balances under a green 'synced' badge
medium_low.evidence: A failed getNep17Balances is recorded as neo:0/gas:0 with only console.warn; the load only errors if EVERY address fails. Totals understate with no per-wallet indicator and the hero still says 'Live balances synced'.
medium_low.fix: Carry failedCount (and per-wallet failed flag) into TreasuryData; show a '{n} wallets unreachable' warning chip in the group header and mark failed rows with an em-dash instead of 0.

medium_low.title: Price-feed failure blanks the entire dashboard even though balances are fetchable
medium_low.evidence: fetchTreasuryData awaits fetchPrices() before any balance fetch; a Morpheus DataFeed read failure throws and (with empty cache) the whole load fails with 'Failed to fetch live prices…' — NEO/GAS balances never render. On testnet sessions this is the live behavior risk: the testnet feed is frozen (verified: last update 2026-03-09).
medium_low.fix: Wrap fetchPrices in try/catch; on failure proceed with balances and set totalUsd/category.totalUsd to null, rendering USD as '—' with a 'price feed unavailable' note.

medium_low.title: Chinese locale prefixes USD values with ¥
medium_low.evidence: currencySymbol: { en: "$", zh: "¥" } while totalUsd is always a USD figure and the label is '总美元' (Total USD) — zh users see '¥4,123,456' for a dollar amount.
medium_low.fix: Set currencySymbol zh to "$" (or render 'US$'); the value is denominated in USD regardless of locale.

medium_low.title: Watchlist not refreshed after a successful disbursement
medium_low.evidence: submitDisbursement sets lastTxid and status but never re-runs loadData(); a transfer to a watched wallet leaves the dashboard stale until manual Refresh.
medium_low.fix: After result.txid, schedule loadData() with a ~6s delay (RPC node-lag tolerance) and show the refreshing signal.

medium_low.title: Hardcoded '$' in group cards bypasses the currencySymbol i18n key used by the hero
medium_low.evidence: usd: `$${formatNumber(category.totalUsd, 2)}` while the hero metric uses ctx.t('currencySymbol') — two different currency-prefix sources in one screen.
medium_low.fix: Use the same t('currencySymbol') (after fixing the zh value) or a shared formatUsd helper in both places.

medium_low.title: Dead components TreasuryHero.tsx and TreasuryLoadingState.tsx are never imported
medium_low.evidence: grep shows no imports of TreasuryHero/TreasuryLoadingState anywhere in src; PlayArea renders its own hero and uses text placeholders instead of a loading skeleton.
medium_low.fix: Either delete both files or wire TreasuryLoadingState as the initial-load skeleton (it would fill the current 'Live data pending' text-only loading gap).

medium_low.title: Mixed-network display on testnet sessions is unlabeled
medium_low.evidence: Watchlist balances always come from hardcoded mainnet RPC endpoints while the disbursement panel signs on launchContext.network (manifest supports neo-n3-testnet) — a testnet session silently shows mainnet treasury data next to a 'Neo N3 Testnet' wallet strip.
medium_low.fix: Add a small 'Watchlist data: Mainnet' tag to the watchlist section header (the watchlist being mainnet-only is by design; just say so).

purpose: Generate Neo N3 accounts locally and convert WIF/private/public keys, derive addresses, and disassemble NeoVM scripts — all on-device.

journeys.name: Generate new account
journeys.detail: dispatch('generate') → generateAccount() via @r3e/neo-js-sdk PrivateKey, WIF base58check-encoded locally; secrets masked by default with show/hide toggle; success toast via registerActions.

journeys.name: Export paper wallet PDF
journeys.detail: Gated behind secrets reveal with an explanatory note; dynamic qrcode+pdf imports wrapped by registerActions so failures surface a localized toast (paperWalletFailed); throws genEmptyState when no account exists.

journeys.name: Convert WIF / private key / public key
journeys.detail: detectAndConvert auto-detects format in order WIF → public key → private key, derives address/pubkey/WIF, renders labeled result rows with copy buttons (ClipboardService toasts on copy) and a sensitive-value mask.

journeys.name: Disassemble NeoVM script
journeys.detail: Verified the SDK OpCode table is Neo N3 (PUSHINT8=0x00, PUSHDATA1=0x0C, SYSCALL=0x41) — the earlier NEO2-opcode finding is fixed. Framing handles PUSHDATA1/2/4 length prefixes, PUSHINT operand widths, and all fixed-operand opcodes (jumps, SYSCALL, INITSLOT, CONVERT…), with overflow-safe little-endian reads.

journeys.name: Convert a Neo N3 address (promised by the input placeholder)
journeys.detail: Placeholder says 'Enter WIF, hex, or address...' but detectAndConvert has no address branch — pasting an N-address falls through every validator (base58 isn't hex) and errors 'Unknown format'.

journeys.name: View connected-wallet balances
journeys.detail: Balances load on mount only if a wallet is already connected (loadBalances early-returns on empty address) and there is no in-app connect affordance; disconnected users see '0 NEO / 0 GAS' hero stats that read as real zeros.

medium_low.title: Input placeholder promises address conversion that does not exist
medium_low.evidence: enterKeyPlaceholder = 'Enter WIF, hex, or address...' (messages.ts:40-43) but the detection chain is WIF → pubkey → privkey → hex script only; an N3 address yields the 'Unknown format' error toast.
medium_low.fix: Add an address branch: validate base58check version byte 0x35, output the script hash (both 0x big-endian and little-endian forms) via the existing addressToScriptHash util — or reword the placeholder to 'WIF, key, or script hex'.

medium_low.title: Hero shows '0 NEO / 0 GAS' with no wallet connected and no connect affordance
medium_low.evidence: loadBalances() returns early when chain.address is empty, leaving the createObservable(0) defaults rendered as real-looking zero balances.
medium_low.fix: When chain.address is empty render '—' for both stats with a muted 'connect a wallet to see balances' caption, or hide the two balance tiles entirely.

medium_low.title: Format-detection errors never persist inline — only a transient toast
medium_low.evidence: The conversion-status box renders only when hasConversionResult is true, but 'unknownFormat' clears the result — so the error state appears only as a 3s toast and the panel returns to looking untouched.
medium_low.fix: Render the conversion-status box when conversionStatusType === 'error' as well (it already has the --error styling in PlayArea.scss:117-120).

medium_low.title: Missing i18n key loadingBalances falls back to hardcoded English
medium_low.evidence: t('loadingBalances') exists in neither locale/messages.ts nor base-messages.ts, so zh users see the literal fallback 'Loading balances...'.
medium_low.fix: Add loadingBalances: { en: 'Loading balances...', zh: '正在加载余额…' } to locale/messages.ts.

medium_low.title: Disassembler prints raw operand hex instead of decoded values
medium_low.evidence: PUSHINT8..256 operands render as little-endian hex (e.g. 'PUSHINT32 00e1f505' for 100000000) and SYSCALL shows the raw 4-byte interop hash — users must decode by hand.
medium_low.fix: Decode PUSHINT operands to decimal via the existing readLittleEndian/BigInt path and map the ~20 common SYSCALL hashes (System.Contract.Call, System.Crypto.CheckSig…) to names, appending the raw hex in parentheses.

medium_low.title: One showSecrets flag toggles both the generator card and the converter card
medium_low.evidence: Revealing the WIF of a freshly generated account also unmasks any private key sitting in the converter results (and vice versa).
medium_low.fix: Split into showGeneratedSecrets / showConversionSecrets observables wired to their respective toggle buttons.

purpose: Read-only Neo N3 block explorer — network stats, identifier search (tx/address/block/contract), and recent transactions.

journeys.name: View network stats on load
journeys.detail: loadAll on mount: cache-first paint, /api/explorer/stats fetched then polled every 15s via useTicker; null txCount ('unavailable' from indexer) correctly degrades to the '—' pending placeholder via isPendingFigure.

journeys.name: Search tx / address / block / contract
journeys.detail: Search button disabled on empty query with an aria-live inline hint; /api/explorer/search?q=&network= → typed result cards for block/transaction/address/contract incl. contract found:false handling; 404 mapped to a calm 'no results' card; other failures toast via registerActions.

journeys.name: Search an unrecognized or not-found identifier
journeys.detail: The API returns {type:'unknown'} for malformed queries and {type:'transaction'|'block'|'address', found:false} for valid-shaped-but-missing ones; SearchResultDisplay has no branch for 'unknown' (section renders title with no card) and renders tx/block/address cards with entirely blank values when found:false — both look broken to the user.

journeys.name: Browse recent transactions and click into one
journeys.detail: Recent list loads at mount and on network toggle with a quality empty-state guidance card; clicking a tx pipes its hash into search (viewTx). But the list is never polled — it goes permanently stale while the block-height metric keeps ticking next to it.

journeys.name: Toggle mainnet/testnet
journeys.detail: Toggle re-scopes stats figures and reloads recent txs (selectedNetwork.subscribe), but the previous network's search result stays on screen and the shared tx cache key first paints the other network's transactions.

medium_low.title: Recent transactions never refresh after mount
medium_low.evidence: Only loadStats is wired to the 15s useTicker; loadRecentTxs runs once in loadAll and on network toggle, so the 'Recent Transactions' lane shows the same 10 txs forever while the height metric beside it keeps incrementing.
medium_low.fix: Add loadRecentTxs to the poll (same ticker or a second 30s ticker); the existing isLoadingTxs guard already prevents overlap.

medium_low.title: No Enter-to-submit on the search input (shared NeoInput has no key handling)
medium_low.evidence: grep for onEnter/onKeyDown/keydown in NeoInput.tsx returns nothing — pressing Enter in the explorer search box (SearchPanel.tsx:36-41), the most search-shaped input in the fleet, does nothing; users must click the button. Same gap affects neo-convert's converter input.
medium_low.fix: Add an optional onEnter prop to NeoInput (onKeyDown Enter → onEnter()) and wire SearchPanel's NeoInput onEnter={onSearch} (guarded by isEmptyQuery).

medium_low.title: Recent-tx cache key is shared across networks
medium_low.evidence: TXS_CACHE_KEY='explorer_txs_cache' regardless of selectedNetwork — toggling to testnet first paints cached mainnet transactions (and the mount paint can show whichever network was viewed last).
medium_low.fix: Key the cache per network: `explorer_txs_cache:${selectedNetwork.get()}` for both read and write.

medium_low.title: Stale search result persists across network toggle
medium_low.evidence: selectedNetwork.subscribe only reloads recent txs; a mainnet contract result stays rendered after switching to testnet with nothing indicating which network it came from.
medium_low.fix: In the same subscription, searchResult.set(null) so the metrics-strip 'Search result' tile resets to '—'.

medium_low.title: Initial stats load shows the 'Searching…' label
medium_low.evidence: The single spinner block renders t('searching') for both isSearching and isLoading — during first mount the user sees 'Searching…' before they have typed anything.
medium_low.fix: Use isSearching ? t('searching') : t('loading') for the spinner label.

purpose: Security checklist, safety score, and balance insights for your Neo wallet, with an exportable health report.

journeys.name: Connect wallet
journeys.detail: connectWallet → chain.ensureWallet() with an isConnecting in-flight guard against duplicate popups; on success immediately refreshes balances; errors re-thrown so registerActions toasts them.

journeys.name: View balances on open (wallet already connected)
journeys.detail: loadData checks health.address.value — verified valid: ChainService wraps address with withValueCompat (ChainService.ts:132-139) so .value works — then refreshBalances reads NEO+GAS balanceOf concurrently via chain.read against native contracts.

journeys.name: Refresh balances
journeys.detail: Button disabled until connected and while refreshing; failures re-throw so the user gets an error toast instead of silently stale figures.

journeys.name: Complete security checklist / see score and risk verdict
journeys.detail: 5 manual items toggle and persist synchronously under the app-namespaced runtime-cache key 'miniapp-wallet-health:checklist'; the GAS item is auto-derived (>=0.1 GAS); score ring (conic-gradient) and risk chip re-derive correctly through the revision observable.

journeys.name: Act on recommendations
journeys.detail: Recommendations derive from only 3 of the 6 checklist dimensions (backup/gas/permissions) — once those are done the panel declares 'All checks look good' even while device/hardware/2FA items are pending and the risk chip still says Medium.

journeys.name: Export health report (copy address / copy report / download .txt)
journeys.detail: Report assembles all stats + checklist + recommendations with an aria-live status line for copied/downloaded/error states; download via Blob+ObjectURL with cleanup.

medium_low.title: Pre-connect state shows an alarming computed risk verdict and zero balances
medium_low.evidence: With no wallet connected the auto 'gas' item evaluates gasOk on the 0n default → checklist shows it failed, recommendations include 'top up GAS', the score ring reads low/'High risk', and NEO/GAS tiles show '0'/'0.0000' as if they were real balances.
medium_low.fix: Gate the auto gas item and the gas recommendation on isConnected (render it as 'connect to check' / excluded from the score denominator), and display '—' for NEO/GAS while disconnected.

medium_low.title: 'All checks look good' contradicts an incomplete checklist
medium_low.evidence: recommendations only inspects checklistState.backup, gasOk, and checklistState.permissions; with those three done, visibleRecommendations falls back to t('allSet') while device/hardware/twofa remain pending and riskLabel still shows Medium (score 67%).
medium_low.fix: Derive recommendations from every unchecked item (add recommendationDevice/Hardware/2fa keys), so the panel and the score/risk chip always agree.

medium_low.title: Report actions bypass the shared ClipboardService
medium_low.evidence: copyText uses navigator.clipboard.writeText directly and throws when unavailable — losing ClipboardService's execCommand fallback (which matters inside the sandboxed iframe) and its standardized toast channel; failures collapse to a generic 'Action failed'.
medium_low.fix: Expose ctx.services.clipboard through an action (like neo-convert's 'copy' action) and dispatch it, keeping the local aria-live label for the report-specific states.

medium_low.title: Exported report mixes locales and drops the % on the score
medium_low.evidence: Report lines hardcode 'DONE'/'PENDING' English markers regardless of locale, and `${t('statScore')}: ${safetyScore}` prints '安全评分: 67' without the % used everywhere else in the UI.
medium_low.fix: Add reportDone/reportPending message keys and append '%' to the score line (`${safetyScore}%`).

medium_low.title: Host-side wallet connection while the app is open doesn't refresh balances
medium_low.evidence: Data loaders only run at lifecycle mount (LifecycleService.ts:170-172) and the app never subscribes to chain.address — if the wallet connects via the host after the app is open, balances and the auto gas check stay at 0 until the user presses Refresh.
medium_low.fix: In setup, subscribe to ctx.services.chain.address and call health.refreshBalances() when it transitions from empty to set (mirror neo-treasury main.tsx:141).

purpose: Seal a message hash on-chain with a refundable 0.2 GAS deposit until a future unlock date; reveal returns the deposit; others can 'fish' your public capsules for a 0.05 GAS tip.

journeys.name: seal capsule (deposit + bury)
journeys.detail: Form validates title/content/days (1-3650), sha256s content locally, then invokes a raw GAS transfer with memo 'miniapp-timecapsule:bury' followed IMMEDIATELY by bury() with no deposit-settlement wait (useTimeCapsule.ts:539-565). If bury lands before the deposit credit, it faults and the user sees 'deposit prepaid but capsule not buried' — the exact race ChainService.prepayAndInvoke (ChainService.ts:552-595) was built to eliminate via waitForDepositConfirmation. Verified deployed contract 0x3e88058e... live on BOTH mainnet and testnet with matching ABI (bury/reveal/getCapsule/getOwnerCapsules).

journeys.name: reveal capsule + reclaim deposit
journeys.detail: Card shows Open button when Date.now() >= unlockTime (recomputed per render, PlayArea.tsx:170-176); openCapsule re-checks live then invokes reveal(owner,id) with waitForEvent 'Revealed'; deposit returns atomically; list reloads and the revealed card shows the locally stored message.

journeys.name: fish another user's public capsule
journeys.detail: fishCapsule scans up to 200 capsules, picks the newest other-owner public one, sends 0.05 GAS with memo 'miniapp-timecapsule:fish:<id>'. The tx works on-chain, but ALL user feedback is dead: fishResult/fishNone are emitted on eventBus channel 'capsule:fished' (useTimeCapsule.ts:670,697) which nothing listens to — MiniAppRoot only handles 'platform:notification' (MiniAppRoot.tsx:305-312) and the action registers no successKey. The fisher pays real GAS, sees no toast, and the owner-scoped list reload shows nothing new. When no candidate exists, the button spins and stops with zero feedback.

journeys.name: withdraw stranded prepaid credit
journeys.detail: The deployed contract exposes creditOf(owner) and withdraw(account) (verified on-chain at 0x3e88058e...), and the failure copy tells users their 0.2 GAS 'is held on the contract as reusable credit' — but no UI ever reads creditOf or offers withdraw. Money-in without money-out UI; the composable doc even claims 'there is no refund call' (useTimeCapsule.ts:39-41), which is stale.

journeys.name: view capsule list + status
journeys.detail: getOwnerCapsules + per-id getCapsule, newest first, locked/ready/revealed badges, category chips, list refreshes after create/open. Empty state distinguishes no-capsules vs no-local-capsules.

medium_low.title: No withdraw UI for prepaid credit despite contract support
medium_low.evidence: Deployed ABI (0x3e88058e…, verified via getcontractstate on testnet) includes creditOf(owner) and withdraw(account) with CreditWithdrawn event, but the app never reads creditOf nor exposes withdraw; depositPrepaidNoCapsule copy parks funds with 'just try sealing again' as the only exit. Composable comment 'there is no refund call (and none is needed)' is stale.
medium_low.fix: On loadAll, read creditOf(ownerHash); when > 0 show a banner ('You have X GAS reusable deposit credit') with a Withdraw button dispatching chainService.invoke('withdraw', [owner], { waitForEvent: 'CreditWithdrawn' }).

medium_low.title: Fish scan fires up to 200 parallel RPC reads per click
medium_low.evidence: loadPublicCandidates builds ids for the newest MAX_SCAN=200 capsules and does Promise.all(ids.map(readCapsule)) — 200 concurrent invokefunction calls on every fish attempt, even though only the first match is used.
medium_low.fix: Scan newest-first in chunks of 10-20 with early exit once a fishable candidate is found; optionally cache getCapsule results for revealed/fished ids.

medium_low.title: Locked capsules show no countdown; timeRemaining i18n keys are dead
medium_low.evidence: Cards show only 'Unlocks: <date>' and 'Not unlocked yet'; messages.ts defines timeRemaining/daysShort/hoursShort/minShort (lines 13,37-39) that no component renders, and nothing re-renders at the unlock moment without user interaction.
medium_low.fix: Render a remaining-time chip (Xd Yh Zm) from unlockTime using the existing keys, driven by a 60s interval that also flips locked→ready at the boundary.

medium_low.title: Revealing a capsule with no local copy gives no hash fallback in the UI
medium_low.evidence: The contentUnavailable+hash message rides the dead 'capsule:opened' eventBus channel, and the revealed card only renders cap.content when non-empty (PlayArea.tsx:207-209) — a capsule revealed on a new device shows a bare 'Revealed' badge with no explanation.
medium_low.fix: In the revealed card, when content is empty but contentHash exists, render t('contentUnavailable') plus the truncated hash; surface the reveal message via ctx.setStatus instead of eventBus.

purpose: Pay a small GAS fee to permanently bury an encrypted content hash on-chain, with an optional paid 'forget' state change later.

journeys.name: bury memory (testnet)
journeys.detail: Hash input (≥12 chars, printable-ASCII validated before payment), memory-type picker, review panel with live on-chain buryFee, two-step confirm on the CTA, then chain.invokeWithPayment(buryFee, 'miniapp-graveyard:memory', 'buryMemory', …) with deposit-settlement polling and waitForEvent MemoryBuried; optimistic prepend + full reload. Verified against testnet contract 0xb55aa635 ABI (onNEP17Payment + buryMemory(owner,contentHash,memoryType)).

journeys.name: bury memory (mainnet — the default network)
journeys.detail: Manifest default_network=neo-n3-mainnet points at 0x0195e668…, verified on-chain to be the OLD kernel generation: buryMemory takes (owner, contentHash, memoryType, receiptId) — 4 params vs the app's 3 — and the contract has NO onNEP17Payment, so the invokeWithPayment deposit transfer itself faults. Both paid journeys fail for every mainnet user.

journeys.name: forget memory
journeys.detail: Testnet flow is correct (invokeWithPayment + MemoryForgotten + in-place flag update), but the Forget button in HistoryTab fires the paid flow with NO confirmation and NO fee display — forgetting costs 1 GAS, 10x the burial fee; forgetFee is loaded from getPlatformStats but never exposed to the UI. Mainnet: broken (same old-contract mismatch).

journeys.name: review burial history
journeys.detail: Rebuilt from MemoryBuried events (limit 200) filtered to the wallet, enriched with getMemoryDetails for live forgotten state; manual Refresh button; loading state on it. Caps at 20 rows displayed while the Buried counter can exceed it.

journeys.name: add epitaph to a buried memory
journeys.detail: Both deployed contracts expose addEpitaph and getMemoryDetails returns an epitaph field, and the manifest's host operation panel lists 'Add Epitaph' — but the in-app UI has no epitaph input anywhere and never renders existing epitaphs in HistoryTab. The in-app journey the contract supports does not exist.

medium_low.title: Burial requires a pre-made content hash the app never helps create
medium_low.evidence: The only input is 'Enter encrypted content hash...' (assetHashPlaceholder); validation is length>=12 + printable ASCII. A first-time user has no in-app way to produce a hash of their memory — unlike sister app time-capsule, which sha256s the message locally.
medium_low.fix: Add a 'write the memory, we hash it locally' mode: textarea → sha256Hex(content) (shared utils/hash) shown as the burial target, with the raw text never leaving the device — same pattern as time-capsule's createCapsule.

medium_low.title: History caps at 20 rows with no pagination while counters can exceed it
medium_low.evidence: HISTORY_DISPLAY_LIMIT=20 slices the event-derived list; totalDestroyed comes from getUserMemoryCount and can read 35 while the records panel shows 20 with no way to see the rest (and the records stat shows historyCount=20, disagreeing with Buried).
medium_low.fix: Add a 'Show more' button that raises the slice window (events are already fetched up to 200), and footnote the records stat when truncated.

medium_low.title: 'Burial Fees' hero stat is computed as count x current fee, not actual paid amounts
medium_low.evidence: burialFeesPaid.set(Number(formatGasAmount(buryFee.get() * BigInt(userCount)))) — if the contract owner ever changes buryFee, the lifetime total is mispriced for all prior burials.
medium_low.fix: Either label the stat as an estimate in copy, or sum the user's actual deposits from the Credited/MemoryBuried event log.

medium_low.title: Epitaph feature exists on-chain but has no in-app UI
medium_low.evidence: Both deployed contracts expose addEpitaph(memoryId, epitaph) and getMemoryDetails returns an epitaph field (read in useGraveyard.ts loadHistory enrichment but discarded); the manifest operation_panel advertises 'Add Epitaph' yet PlayArea/HistoryTab have no epitaph input or display.
medium_low.fix: Render the epitaph (when set) on each history card and add a small 'Add epitaph' inline action invoking chain.invoke('addEpitaph', [id, text]) — it is a free, non-deposit call.

purpose: Create permanent on-chain memorials for the deceased and pay GAS-priced tribute offerings (incense to feast, 0.01-0.5 GAS) at them.

journeys.name: create memorial
journeys.detail: Free createMemorial(creator, name, photoHash, relationship, birthYear, deathYear, bio, obituary) with waitForEvent MemorialCreated; signature verified IDENTICAL on testnet (0x87f0fe2b) and mainnet (0xee7a548b) via live getcontractstate. Good inline year validation (digits, not-future, birth<=death) and notify.guard success/error toasts; catalog reloads after.

journeys.name: pay tribute (testnet)
journeys.detail: invokeWithPayment(offeringCost, 'miniapp-memorial-shrine:tribute:…', 'payTribute', …) with deposit-confirmation polling and TributePaid wait; cost card shows the selected offering price before signing; optimistic myTributes record then full reconcile.

journeys.name: pay tribute (mainnet — the default network)
journeys.detail: Mainnet payTribute has a 5th receiptId param (old PaymentHub generation, no onNEP17Payment), so the app demands a manually-typed 'Payment receipt ID' (PlayArea.tsx:233-240). There is no in-app flow that produces a receipt — a normal user cannot complete the journey on the app's default network; only the host's operation panel (which batches payment+call via invokeMultiple) works.

journeys.name: see tribute impact on a memorial
journeys.detail: The contract tracks per-offering tallies (incenseCount…feastCount) and the composable parses them into Memorial.offerings plus full myTributes records — but NOTHING renders them: TombstoneCard shows name/years/relationship only, the detail card shows bio + form only, and myTributes surfaces solely as a count. Paying 0.01-0.5 GAS produces no visible change beyond 'Tributes: +1'.

journeys.name: browse memorials, obituary banner, deep link
journeys.detail: Catalog from getMemorialCount + per-id reads (newest first, cap 60), obituary banner from getRecentObituaries, ?id= deep link honored on load and synced via replaceState on open/close.

journeys.name: share memorial
journeys.detail: navigator.share with title/text/url; on desktop browsers without Web Share the button silently does nothing — no clipboard fallback, and the shareStatus observable is never set.

medium_low.title: 'Visited' stat is fabricated — seeded with the first two catalog memorials on every load
medium_low.evidence: loadVisitedMemorials() does visitedMemorials.set(memorials.get().slice(0, 2)) 'so the stat is populated on first load' — the hero shows Visited=2 for a user who has opened nothing, and real visits then mix with the fake seeds.
medium_low.fix: Start empty and persist actual openMemorial ids in localStorage (readCachedJSON/writeCachedJSON), rehydrating on load.

medium_low.title: photoHash is collected at create but no photo is ever displayed
medium_low.evidence: The create form asks for 'Photo Hash — IPFS hash or HTTPS URL' (PlayArea.tsx:257) and it is stored on-chain, but TombstoneCard and the detail card never render memorial.photoHash — users prepare an IPFS upload for nothing.
medium_low.fix: Render the photo when photoHash is an https:// URL or via an IPFS gateway (ipfs.io/ipfs/<hash>) with the heart icon as fallback on error; otherwise drop the field from the form.

medium_low.title: Share silently no-ops without Web Share API
medium_low.evidence: if (navigator.share) … with no else branch — on desktop the Share button does nothing; shareStatus observable and its cleanup timer exist but are never used.
medium_low.fix: Fallback to navigator.clipboard.writeText(shareUrl) and toast 'Link copied' via ctx.services.notify; remove the dead shareStatus plumbing or wire it.

medium_low.title: Catalog and tribute loads fan out as unbounded parallel reads
medium_low.evidence: loadMemorials Promise.alls up to 60 getMemorialDetails calls; loadMyTributes nests getMemorialTributes + per-tribute getTributeDetails (up to 50 per memorial) — hundreds of concurrent RPC calls for an active visitor.
medium_low.fix: Chunk reads (10 concurrent), reuse chainService.readCached for memorial details, and only re-read the tributed memorial after payTribute instead of the full catalog.

purpose: A wallet-scoped on-chain photo vault: upload up to 5 small images (optionally AES-GCM encrypted locally) as wallet-signed storage records and view them forever.

journeys.name: upload photos
journeys.detail: Each photo's storageService.set() returns a kernel putMiniAppState intent which EdgeClient AUTO-SUBMITS via wallet.invokeWithConfirmation (EdgeClient.ts:170-210, audit fix E-1/H-3), then the composable's submitWriteIntent re-invokes the SAME intent via chainService.invoke (useForeverAlbum.ts:229-236,441) — two confirmation prompts and two duplicate paid transactions per photo (x5 photos + NFT marker + rollback deletes). On the manifest's default network (mainnet) it fails outright: the registry kernel hash 0x4b882e94 is 'Unknown contract' on three independent mainnet RPCs. No GAS cost disclosure either — a 45KB photo costs on the order of 45 GAS in storage fees at sign time.

journeys.name: view album after upload or reload
journeys.detail: loadPhotos → storageService.list(prefix) → edge returns intent {operation:'getMiniAppState', args:[appId, prefixBytes], meta:{list:true}}. EdgeClient first auto-signs this READ as a transaction (confirmation modal + network fee on every album load), then the composable's resolveReadIntent drops meta and does an exact-key chainService.read of getMiniAppState(appId, '<bare prefix>') — verified on-chain (testnet kernel 0xf54d8584) that getMiniAppState(appId, stateKey)->ByteArray is single-key. Photos are stored at prefix+id, so the bare-prefix read always returns nothing: the gallery is permanently empty even after a fully successful upload.

journeys.name: decrypt an encrypted photo
journeys.detail: Depends on the (always-empty) photo list to select a target; additionally a wrong password is swallowed silently — handleDecrypt catches its own error and emits 'album:error' on a dead eventBus channel (useForeverAlbum.ts:318-321), so the notify.guard errorKey in main.tsx never fires and the user gets no feedback.

journeys.name: select and validate images before upload
journeys.detail: File picker, per-image 45KB and total 60KB gates, encrypted-size estimator that mirrors the AES-GCM envelope growth, live payload meter, removable thumbnails, readiness line on the footer — all good. But rejection feedback (imageTooLarge, maxPhotosReached) emits on the dead 'album:error' channel, so an oversized image silently never appears in the selection.

medium_low.title: Validation and decrypt errors are silent — emitted on a dead eventBus channel
medium_low.evidence: addFiles emits 'album:error' for maxPhotosReached/imageTooLarge and handleDecrypt catches the wrong-password error internally and emits 'album:error' — no listener exists (MiniAppRoot handles only platform:notification), and because handleDecrypt does not rethrow, the notify.guard errorKey 'decryptFailed' in main.tsx:62-68 never fires. Oversized images vanish silently; wrong passwords give zero feedback.
medium_low.fix: Set the already-rendered uploadError observable for addFiles rejections, and let handleDecrypt rethrow (remove its internal catch) so notify.guard surfaces decryptFailed; add a decryptError line in the decrypt card.

medium_low.title: Album reads trigger wallet confirmation modals
medium_low.evidence: submitWalletIntentIfPresent cannot distinguish read intents (getMiniAppState) from writes, so loadPhotos on every mount/refresh pops 'confirm OS-binder invocation' and, on accept, submits a paid transaction for a pure read. (Shared-component issue, reported once here where most visible — it affects every os.storage/os.nft consumer.)
medium_low.fix: Have edge read endpoints mark intents readonly (meta.readonly=true) and route those through wallet.invokeRead / chainService.read in EdgeClient instead of invokeWithConfirmation.

purpose: Create events, issue attendee NEP-11 ticket passes, and run door check-in (manifest promises QR-based gate verification).

journeys.name: Create event
journeys.detail: Form → dispatch createEvent → useEventTicket.createEvent → chain.invoke('createEvent', [Hash160 creator, name, venue, startTime, endTime, maxSupply, notes]) — matches deployed ABI at 0x90bad472 exactly. Validates name/time-range/supply with localized errors, waits for EventCreated, refreshes list, auto-selects new event. Solid.

journeys.name: Issue ticket to attendee
journeys.detail: Desk tab → issueTicket(creator, recipient, eventId, seat, memo) matches ABI; guards inactive/sold-out/invalid-recipient; waits TicketIssued; refreshes events+tickets and optimistically merges the new ticket. Works end-to-end (contract smoke-tested per manifest deployment note).

journeys.name: Attendee views their tickets ('My Tickets')
journeys.detail: refreshTickets reads tokensOf(owner) which returns an InteropInterface session iterator. Live RPC against api.n3index.dev confirms the node returns {type:'InteropInterface', interface:'IIterator', id:...} with NO items; parseStackItem (apps/shared/utils/neo.ts:142) returns typed.value = undefined; /api/rpc/neo doesn't allow traverseiterator. Array.isArray(undefined) → [] → the list is permanently empty. Doc step3 ('Attendees open My Tickets and show the token ID QR') is therefore broken.

journeys.name: Door check-in (lookup + checkIn)
journeys.detail: lookupTicket reads getTicketDetails(ByteArray tokenId) → Map (single-item read, no iterator) and renders seat/owner/used badge; checkIn(creator, tokenId) matches ABI, guards already-used, re-resolves stale lookups when the input changed, updates lookup+list optimistically then refreshes. Good flow — but the operator must hand-type token ids (no QR scan/display, see finding).

journeys.name: Pause/resume ticket sales
journeys.detail: toggleEvent → setEventActive(creator, eventId, active) matches ABI, optimistic merge + quiet refresh, per-row loading state via togglingId.

journeys.name: Transfer/gift a ticket
journeys.detail: Contract now exposes standard NEP-11 transfer(to, tokenId, data) (confirmed in contracts/build/MiniAppEventTicketPass.manifest.json) but no UI, action, or composable method calls it. A transferable ticket pass implies this journey; it just shipped on-chain and the app doesn't surface it.

journeys.name: Show ticket QR at the door
journeys.detail: Manifest tag 'qr', check-in placeholder 'Enter token ID from QR', doc step3 promises a token-ID QR — but no QR code is ever rendered anywhere; ticket cards show the raw token id as text only.

medium_low.title: QR journey promised in copy/tags but no QR is rendered or scanned
medium_low.evidence: Locale step3 'Attendees open My Tickets and show the token ID QR', checkinTokenIdPlaceholder 'Enter token ID from QR' (locale/messages.ts:76,119), manifest tag 'qr', and a QrCode icon in the empty check-in state — yet ticket cards print the token id as <code> text only and check-in is manual typing.
medium_low.fix: Render a small inline SVG QR of ticket.tokenId on each ticket-pass card (a dependency-free QR generator in apps/shared/utils would serve both this and soulbound-certificate). At minimum add a copy-token-id button — the locale key copyTokenId already exists unused.

medium_low.title: Primary decoded-events path is dead: n3index events API returns {data,paging} envelope but the client expects a bare array
medium_low.evidence: createEventsComposable.list checks `if (Array.isArray(data))` after fetching <N3INDEX_API>/indexer/v1/networks/<net>/contracts/<hash>/events. Live response is {"data":[...],"paging":{...}} (verified by curl), so the n3index branch never yields events and every waitForEvent (used by createEvent/issueTicket/checkIn for eventId/tokenId extraction) silently falls back to the platform API. Reported once here (most visible: createEvent relies on the EventCreated payload to auto-select the new event).
medium_low.fix: Accept both shapes: `const rows = Array.isArray(data) ? data : (Array.isArray(data?.data) ? data.data : null); if (rows) return { events: rows.map(...) }`.

medium_low.title: 418-line orphaned legacy composable and unused EventList component
medium_low.evidence: useEventTicketContract.ts (418 lines, contains copyTokenId/attendance-badge logic) and src/pages/index/components/EventList.tsx are imported by nothing (verified by grep). The locale also carries their dead keys (copyTokenId, issueAttendanceBadge, attendanceTemplateId, etc. at locale/messages.ts:68-78).
medium_low.fix: Delete both files and prune the dead locale keys — or, better, salvage copyTokenId into the live PlayArea ticket cards (pairs with the QR finding).

medium_low.title: Events panel subtitle shows 'Event selected' whenever events exist, even before any selection
medium_low.evidence: `{events.length ? t("eventSelected") : t("emptyEvents")}` — the header always reads 'Event selected' once the list is non-empty, regardless of selection state; it's a status string misused as a panel subtitle.
medium_low.fix: Show the selected event's name (selectedEvent?.name) or a count summary like `${events.length} events`; fall back to t('emptyEvents') when empty.

medium_low.title: Free-text date inputs invite invalidTime errors
medium_low.evidence: eventStart/eventEnd are plain text NeoInputs expecting 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm' (parseDateInput rejects anything Date.parse can't read); the only guidance is a placeholder, and failures surface post-submit as a generic 'Invalid event time range'.
medium_low.fix: Switch to type="datetime-local" inputs (native pickers, guaranteed parseable values) and keep parseDateInput as the safety net.

purpose: Issuers publish certificate templates and mint non-transferable NEP-11 credentials; recipients display them and anyone can verify/revoke by token ID.

journeys.name: Create template
journeys.detail: Form (prefilled sensibly) → createTemplate(issuer, name, issuerName, category, maxSupply, description) matches deployed ABI at 0x4e920c7f; client-side validation mirrors contract bounds (supply 1-100000); waits TemplateCreated; refreshes list. Good.

journeys.name: Issue certificate
journeys.detail: Template chip picker or manual ID → issueCertificate(issuer, recipient, templateId, recipientName, achievement, memo) matches ABI; address normalized via addressToScriptHash; waits CertificateIssued; auto-verifies the new token and refreshes. Contract asserts template ownership + supply — UI guards exhausted/inactive templates.

journeys.name: Recipient views 'My Certificates'
journeys.detail: loadCertificatesFromChain reads tokensOf(owner) → InteropInterface session iterator (same root cause as event-ticket-pass, confirmed live) → undefined → certificates.set([]) and early-return. The storage fallback only runs on throw, and an empty set isn't a throw, so it never engages. The list and the hero certificatesCount metric are permanently 0/empty despite tokens() now working contract-side.

journeys.name: Verify certificate by token ID
journeys.detail: getCertificateDetails(ByteArray) → Map verified live on testnet (token '1-1' returns full record; base64 ByteStrings decode to readable text via parseByteLike). Status strip honestly reports Revoked vs Valid. Solid — except the issued/revoked timestamps render wrong (see finding).

journeys.name: Revoke certificate
journeys.detail: revokeCertificate(issuer, tokenId) matches ABI and re-verifies after; but the Revoke button is rendered for every verifier on any valid cert — the contract only lets the template issuer revoke, so recipients/third parties hit a wallet prompt then an on-chain 'not issuer' assert.

journeys.name: Share issue link with deep-link prefill
journeys.detail: Copy/Share builds ?issueTemplateId=N&autoIssueDraft=1; on open the Issue panel prefills and scrolls (nice mechanics). But issueCertificate asserts data.Issuer == issuer on-chain (MiniAppSoulboundCertificate.Methods.cs:132), so anyone except the original issuer who follows the shared link fills the form and gets an unauthorized revert. The share affordance (navigator.share to a counterparty) contradicts the issuer-only contract gate.

journeys.name: Recipient displays token-ID QR (doc step3)
journeys.detail: docDescription and step3 promise 'verified by token ID QR' — no QR rendering exists anywhere in the app.

medium_low.title: Revoke button offered to everyone, but only the template issuer can revoke on-chain
medium_low.evidence: `{!verifiedCertificate.revoked && (<NeoButton variant='danger' ... onClick={() => submitRevoke(...)}>` renders for any verifier. RevokeCertificate asserts issuer witness + template ownership, so a recipient verifying their own credential is shown a destructive primary action that can only end in a wallet prompt followed by an 'unauthorized'/'not issuer' revert.
medium_low.fix: Resolve the template issuer (getTemplateDetails(cert.templateId).issuer), compare to the connected address (normalizeHash160), and hide the button otherwise — or disable it with a caption like t('onlyIssuerCanRevoke') (add key en+zh).

medium_low.title: 'Share Issue Link' invites non-issuers into a flow the contract rejects
medium_low.evidence: shareIssueLink uses navigator.share to send ?issueTemplateId&autoIssueDraft to a counterparty, and the receive side prefills the Issue form (PlayArea.tsx:121-143). But IssueCertificate asserts data.Issuer == issuer (Methods.cs:132) — only the template creator's wallet can sign it. Anyone the link is shared WITH completes the form and reverts at the chain.
medium_low.fix: Reframe as an issuer-side bookmark ('Copy issuing shortcut') OR build the journey recipients actually need: a verify deep-link (?verifyTokenId=…) that opens the Verify panel prefilled — buildMiniAppUrl already supports arbitrary params and the verify read is permissionless.

medium_low.title: Desktop layout is an unstyled single column — .certificate-workspace has no CSS
medium_low.evidence: className="certificate-workspace" appears nowhere in PlayArea.scss or the theme file (grep confirms only the TSX reference), so Issue / Templates / Create / Verify / My Certificates render as five stacked full-width cards even on wide viewports — a long scroll wall where sibling apps (event-ticket-pass .ticket-workspace) use a responsive two-column grid.
medium_low.fix: Add `.certificate-workspace { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) minmax(0,1fr); gap: 16px; } @media (max-width: 900px) { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }` and let the two .certificate-stack columns sit beside the issue panel.

medium_low.title: ~25 dead locale keys from a removed 'credential draft/registry' feature
medium_low.evidence: registryTitle, draftReadyTitle/Text, draftCredentialType, recommendedTemplates*, recentLinksTitle/Empty, createEventTemplatePreset, etc. are referenced by no TSX/composable (the drafts feature was removed); they inflate the bundle and mislead translators.
medium_low.fix: Delete the unused keys (grep each against src/ before removal).

purpose: SHA-256 timestamp journal and proof lookup — implicitly, prove a piece of content existed at a point in time.

journeys.name: Create a proof entry
journeys.detail: Textarea → createProof → SHA-256 via crypto.subtle → persisted to localStorage (cap 200, sanitized, id auto-increment). Input preserved on failure (nice touch, PlayArea.tsx:75-85), success toast, entry appears immediately. Flawless as a local journal.

journeys.name: Verify/lookup a proof
journeys.detail: Lookup by numeric id, 64-hex digest, or exact original content (useTimestampProof.ts:163-188); stale 'Invalid Proof' error cleared on edit; result card shows id/time/digest/content preview. Works — but it is a journal lookup, not cryptographic verification (see finding).

journeys.name: Copy digest / copy reference JSON, delete, clear all
journeys.detail: All wired with per-action toasts; deleting the currently-verified proof clears the result panel; clear-all resets state. Tidy lifecycle.

journeys.name: Prove existence to a third party (the namesake journey)
journeys.detail: Nothing anchors the digest+time outside this device: no chain write, no contract, no OTS-style anchor. localStorage is user-editable, so any timestamp can be fabricated; the copied 'reference' JSON carries a fake tx-looking field txHash:'local:<hash>'. A counterparty has no way to check anything. The manifest still declares invoke:primary + read:blockchain and the platform ships a free 0-GAS-self-transfer broadcast pattern one app over (neo-sign-anything), so the anchor is one invoke away.

medium_low.title: Fake tx-hash-shaped field in the exportable reference JSON
medium_low.evidence: buildReference copies JSON containing `txHash: "local:1a2b3c..."` — a key named txHash holding a synthetic value. A recipient of this 'proof reference' can reasonably mistake it for an on-chain transaction reference and try to look it up.
medium_low.fix: Rename the key to `localRef` (locale key localReference already exists) or omit it until a real anchoring txid exists; include `"anchored": false` so the artifact is self-describing.

medium_low.title: Stats redundancy: Total Proofs and Your Proofs are always the identical number, shown twice
medium_low.evidence: myProofsCount is defined as proofs.length (useTimestampProof.ts:109-112, deliberately), so the 'Total Proofs' and 'Your Proofs' tiles always match — and the same three figures repeat in the hero facts row (ProofHero.tsx:29-43) directly above the tiles.
medium_low.fix: Drop one of the duplicate stat surfaces (keep the tiles, remove hero-facts or vice-versa) and replace 'Your Proofs' with something informative, e.g. 'Last created' time or 'Anchored' count once anchoring exists.

medium_low.title: Fallback copy over-claims 'immutable timestamp proof'
medium_low.evidence: Hardcoded fallback placeholder reads 'Enter text, hash, or data to create an immutable timestamp proof...' — the locale key (contentPlaceholder) says something different and honest, but the fallback both diverges from the locale and overstates a localStorage entry as 'immutable'.
medium_low.fix: Align the fallback with the locale string ('Paste your text, document hash, or idea...') — fallbacks should mirror en values verbatim.

purpose: Sign any message with your Neo address (zh: messages OR files) and optionally publish it on-chain via a 0-GAS self-transfer for public proof.

journeys.name: Sign a message off-chain
journeys.detail: Textarea → signMessage → chain.signMessage (auto-connects via ensureWallet, ChainService.ts:307-317) → wallet prompt → signature shown truncated + copyable. Mechanically works; but the produced artifact is incomplete for its stated purpose (see verify journey).

journeys.name: Verify a signature (promised by step4/verifyText/docFeature4)
journeys.detail: No verify UI exists, and the copied artifact cannot be verified externally either: the app keeps only the signature hex (publicKey discarded at useSignAnything.ts:52-61); the wallet-sdk drops the salt that NeoLine-class wallets prepend (wallet-sdk.ts:756-762 maps {pubkey, signature} only); and the actual signed payload is base64(message) (encodeBase64Utf8 at wallet-sdk.ts:752-754) — an encoding detail no third-party verifier would guess. The locale explicitly promises 'use your Neo address, the message, and the signature in any verifier' — that recipe fails.

journeys.name: Broadcast message on-chain
journeys.detail: 0-amount GAS transfer to self with the message as the data arg (useSignAnything.ts:95-104), 1024-byte cap enforced with localized error, txid surfaced and copyable, counter persisted via ctx.os.storage. Valid N3 pattern; works.

journeys.name: Broadcast a SIGNED message (sign-then-anchor)
journeys.detail: Sign and broadcast are disjoint: broadcasting embeds the plain message, never the signature, and each action clears the other's result (signature.set('') / txHash.set('')), so the natural journey 'sign it, then anchor the signed proof' cannot be completed or even displayed.

journeys.name: Sign a file (zh manifest: 对任意消息或文件进行链上数字签名)
journeys.detail: No file input exists anywhere; only the textarea.

medium_low.title: Sign and broadcast results clear each other while the UI shows both slots side-by-side
medium_low.evidence: signMessage does signature.set('')+txHash.set(''); broadcastMessage does txHash.set('')+signature.set('') (lines 89-90). The result panel renders Signature and Transaction Hash boxes simultaneously (PlayArea.tsx:138-161), implying both artifacts of the same message can coexist — but completing the second action wipes the first, so a user who signs then broadcasts loses the signature they just produced.
medium_low.fix: Only clear the artifact being regenerated (sign clears signature, broadcast clears txHash); keep both visible when both exist for the current message, and clear both only when the message text changes.

medium_low.title: zh manifest promises file signing; no file input exists
medium_low.evidence: description_zh: '对任意消息或文件进行链上数字签名' (sign any message or FILE) while description (en) and the entire UI are message-only — Chinese users are promised a journey that does not exist.
medium_low.fix: Either align description_zh to the en scope, or add a file picker that SHA-256-hashes the file locally (crypto.subtle, same as timestamp-proof) and signs/broadcasts the digest — which also keeps payloads under the 1024-byte cap.

medium_low.title: Localized status text written into the copyable txHash field
medium_low.evidence: `txHash.set(result.txid || t("txPending"))` — when the wallet returns no txid, the txHash observable holds 'Transaction sent (ID pending)'; the Copy transaction hash button then copies that prose string as if it were a hash.
medium_low.fix: Keep txHash empty when txid is missing and surface pending state via a separate status flag; disable the copy button until a real hash exists.

medium_low.title: Fee opacity: '0 GAS' panel implies free broadcasting; hardcoded English 'bytes' suffix
medium_low.evidence: Line 99 renders `{messageBytes}/1024 bytes` (untranslated 'bytes' shown to zh users) and the safety panel shows 'Transfer amount: 0 GAS' (lines 193-196) with no mention that the broadcast tx still costs network+system fees (~0.01+ GAS), which larger data payloads increase.
medium_low.fix: Localize the byte counter (add key bytesUnit en/zh) and add a fee hint row, e.g. t('networkFeeNote'): 'Broadcast pays normal Neo network fees (~0.01–0.05 GAS depending on size)'.

purpose: Encrypted and time-locked messaging on Neo X: recipient-only messages decrypted via Morpheus oracle signature proof, or time-locked messages revealed publicly on-chain after an unlock time.

journeys.name: connect wallet & load inbox/outbox
journeys.detail: loadData silently restores an authorized EVM account (eth_accounts) and loads inboxOf/outboxOf; manual Connect button covers first-run. Selectors 0x6d9e384b/0x802c8fa0 verified against keccak and the deployed contract 0xd1906192… responds (read-only smoke PASS via deploy/scripts/live_validate_neo_message.mjs).

journeys.name: send recipient-only message
journeys.detail: validateCompose → live oracle public key (verified: https://oracle.meshmini.app/mainnet/oracle/public-key returns the X25519 key) → X25519-HKDF-AES-GCM envelope → sendMessage(address,bytes,uint64=0); selector 0x0759f73a and MessageSent topic verified against on-chain logs. Form resets and lists refresh after the receipt.

journeys.name: recipient decrypts a sealed message
journeys.detail: personal_sign over the canonical reveal statement → POST /oracle/message-reveal; the lane is live (recipient-only e2e in the validator) and the recipient gate (addressesEqual check + server-side signature proof) is enforced. Plaintext stays local, never written on-chain.

journeys.name: send time-locked message
journeys.detail: datetime-local → unlockTime seconds; past dates and invalid dates rejected with locale-keyed errors. Validator proved the full lane on mainnet (message #4 revealed on-chain).

journeys.name: trigger timed on-chain reveal
journeys.detail: requestReveal (0x40261cdd, RevealRequested topic 0xec2bedc1… matches actual on-chain logs) then polls getMessage every 5s for up to 3 minutes while busyId disables ALL other reveal buttons; if the relayer takes >3 min the row goes stale until a manual Refresh.

journeys.name: re-read a previously decrypted message
journeys.detail: Recipient-reveal plaintext is held only in the in-memory inbox row; any refresh re-reads chain state (revealed=false) and wipes it, forcing a new wallet signature + oracle round-trip every session.

journeys.name: arrive on Neo N3 / wrong EVM chain
journeys.detail: detectNetwork returns non-EVM → app shows a static warning and Connect throws errorWrongNetwork; it never attempts wallet_switchEthereumChain even though shared ensureNeoXNetwork can switch/add Neo X automatically.

medium_low.title: Wrong-network dead end: no in-app switch to Neo X
medium_low.evidence: ensureNeoX throws errorWrongNetwork whenever ctx.services.chain.detectNetwork() is not already an EVM network; ensureEvmWallet(NEO_X_MAINNET) (which calls ensureNeoXNetwork → wallet_switchEthereumChain/wallet_addEthereumChain) is only reached after the gate passes, so a MetaMask user on Ethereum or an N3-default wallet with an EVM provider is stuck with 'Switch your wallet manually'.
medium_low.fix: In ensureNeoX, when hasEvmWallet() is true, skip the detectNetwork gate and call ctx.services.chain.ensureEvmWallet(NEO_X_MAINNET) directly so the wallet is prompted to switch/add Neo X; reserve the static errorWrongNetwork card for when no EVM provider exists, and add a 'Switch to Neo X' button on the warning card.

medium_low.title: 3-minute reveal poll blocks every other reveal button and goes stale on timeout
medium_low.evidence: requestTimedReveal loops 36×5s with busyId set; PlayArea.tsx:87/103 disables all reveal buttons via disabled={Boolean(busyId)}. After timeout it sets statusRevealPending but nothing ever re-checks, so the revealed plaintext only appears after a manual Refresh.
medium_low.fix: Track busy state per message id (Set<string>) so only the active row is disabled, and after the poll window schedule a low-frequency background recheck (e.g. on visibilitychange + every 30s for 10 min) that patches the row when revealed flips true.

medium_low.title: Decrypted recipient-only plaintext lost on every refresh
medium_low.evidence: revealRecipient patches the inbox observable in memory only; refreshLists() rebuilds rows from chain where revealed=false/plaintext="", so the just-decrypted message reverts to Sealed and needs a new signature + oracle call to re-read.
medium_low.fix: Cache decrypted plaintext in safe-storage keyed by `${MESSAGE_EVM_ADDRESS}:${id}:${recipient}` and overlay it in readMessage/refreshLists for rows where the connected address is the recipient.

medium_low.title: Inbox refresh fans out one eth_call per message with no cap
medium_low.evidence: loadIdsFor decodes the full uint256[] from inboxOf/outboxOf then Promise.all's a getMessage eth_call for every id; a heavy account triggers hundreds of parallel wallet-provider RPCs on every refresh.
medium_low.fix: Slice to the newest 50 ids before fetching (ids are monotonically increasing, so sort desc then slice), render a 'Load older' button that fetches the next page.

medium_low.title: Body length and reveal date only validated at submit
medium_low.evidence: The textarea has no maxLength/counter for the 2000-char MAX_BODY_LENGTH (message-logic.ts:37) and the datetime-local input has no min attribute, so past dates and over-long bodies are accepted until 'Encrypt & send' errors.
medium_low.fix: Add maxLength={2000} plus a live `{len}/2000` counter under the textarea, and set min on the datetime-local input to the current local datetime.

medium_low.title: Delivery-mode toggle lacks focus-visible affordance
medium_low.evidence: .nm-mode-option defines :hover (border + translateY) and .active, but no :focus-visible state — keyboard users tabbing the radiogroup get the default outline-suppressed button with no ring.
medium_low.fix: Add `&:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: var(--ns-focus-ring, 0 0 0 3px rgba(91,110,245,.18)); border-color: $accent; }` to .nm-mode-option.

purpose: Seal private Neo N3 transfer intents (recipient/amount/memo) locally with the Morpheus oracle key and have confidential compute validate them in a TEE — instead of on-chain zk verification.

journeys.name: seal a private transfer intent
journeys.detail: Validation + local X25519-HKDF-AES-GCM encryption work, but the final store step fails live on BOTH networks: the host proxy posts to `${publicApi}/api/confidential/store`, which I verified returns 404 {"error":"not found"} on mainnet and 503 (runtime degraded) on testnet (the UI default). The proxy converts failure to 200 {inline_fallback:true} with no secret_ref, so the app throws 'Morpheus confidential storage is temporarily unavailable'. The only journey the UI exposes cannot complete.

journeys.name: deposit/lock funds for the transfer
journeys.detail: Step 1 of the app's own 'How a confidential transfer settles' explainer ('Deposit or wallet intent — the public side only needs an asset lock or signed payment intent') has no UI, no action, and no contract; manifest.contracts is empty. No GAS/NEO ever moves.

journeys.name: release or refund (settlement)
journeys.detail: Step 4 ('The user submits the returned settlement intent through the wallet') has no implementation — there is no settlement-intent retrieval, no wallet submit, no refund path. The app ends at ciphertext storage, so the headline promise 'private transfer' never completes.

journeys.name: review past sealed intents / check status
journeys.detail: secretRef/commitment/nullifier exist only in component state; navigating away loses them, requestCount resets per mount, and there is no status-lookup or history view.

medium_low.title: Default network 'testnet' targets the one lane that is still degraded
medium_low.evidence: useState("testnet") while https://oracle.meshmini.app/testnet/oracle/public-key returns 503 runtime_temporarily_degraded (verified); only mainnet serves a key. The default-path user fails at the very first fetch with 'Morpheus sealing is unavailable for this network'.
medium_low.fix: Initialize the network from the connected wallet's network (ctx.services.chain.detectNetwork) falling back to mainnet, and ping /oracle/public-key per network to badge each select option as live/degraded.

medium_low.title: Sealed artifacts are not persisted — secretRef is unrecoverable after unmount
medium_low.evidence: submitState (secretRef/noteCommitment/nullifier) lives in useState; leaving the miniapp discards the only reference to the stored ciphertext, and requestCount/lastDigest observables reseed on next mount (main.tsx:14-19). The user has no record their intent exists.
medium_low.fix: Append each successful seal {secretRef, commitment, nullifier, network, asset, ts} to a safe-storage-backed history list and render it as a 'Sealed intents' card with copy buttons; hydrate requestCount/lastDigest from it in loadData.

medium_low.title: Upstream error detail discarded — user always sees the same generic failure
medium_low.evidence: userFacingSealError maps everything in the store phase to one sentence; the proxy's stored.error (e.g. 'not found' vs 'timed out' vs quota) never surfaces, and console.warn drops the error object entirely, making support diagnosis impossible.
medium_low.fix: Append a small muted detail line in the error aside with the upstream_status/error from the inline_fallback body, and pass the caught error to console.warn.

medium_low.title: Commitment stat seeds with 'N/A' instead of an em-dash
medium_low.evidence: lastDigest: createObservable(ctx.t("notAvailable")) renders 'N/A' in the header stat tile (base-messages notAvailable = 'N/A'), which reads like an error state pre-use; the design convention is an em-dash placeholder.
medium_low.fix: Seed lastDigest (and the sealed-requests sidebar value) with "—" via a digestPlaceholder message key, as already done for oracle-seal-console.

purpose: Resolve Morpheus NeoDID documents and build a portable, optionally wallet-signed identity passport payload for relying parties.

journeys.name: resolve DID and build passport payload
journeys.detail: buildPassport → /api/morpheus/neodid/resolve (host route verified present; DID documents are constructed server-side from canonical registry metadata so resolution succeeds even though the live runtime snapshot is degraded — verified /neodid/runtime returns 503 testnet / 400 mainnet, which the lib treats as null and falls back to versionId 'unversioned'). Validation keys (passportInvalidDid etc.) map to clear en+zh messages.

journeys.name: sign passport with wallet
journeys.detail: signPassport canonicalizes the payload, calls ctx.services.chain.signMessage (no tx broadcast), attaches signature/publicKey/address/messageDigest, and updates proof status to Signed with digest shown. Provider gating (passportNoPayload/passportNoWalletProvider) is correct and disabled-state on the Sign button matches.

journeys.name: copy payload for a relying party
journeys.detail: services.clipboard.copy with a 'copied' toast; full pretty-printed JSON visible in the result panel with summary tiles (version/services/digest/signature).

journeys.name: GitHub / email attestation
journeys.detail: Selecting github/email only flips proof.type to ExternalAttestationPrepared with status 'prepared' — there is no journey to actually obtain the attestation (no verifier URL, no upload, no callback). The hint admits it's 'for an external verifier' but the user has nowhere to go next.

journeys.name: build via the auto-generated operation panel
journeys.detail: manifest.operations renders a SECOND copy of the same form in the right sidebar (and on mobile); dispatching from it builds a passport from its own unsynced field values while the center form still shows different values — confusing dual-form state.

medium_low.title: Duplicate form: manifest.operations renders a second unsynced Passport Builder beside the custom one
medium_low.evidence: manifest declares an operations[] entry with the same subject/provider/claim/audience fields the PlayArea form already implements; MiniAppRoot.tsx:553-565 renders MiniAppOperationPanel in the focus-mode right sidebar (page-grid--focus 'center right') and again in .section-mobile-operation on mobile. The two forms hold independent state, so building from the panel shows results that contradict the center form's inputs.
medium_low.fix: Delete the operations array from appConfig.ts (keep stats/sidebar); the custom PlayArea form is the single surface for buildPassport.

medium_low.title: GitHub/email providers dead-end at a 'prepared' stub
medium_low.evidence: proof.type ExternalAttestationPrepared / status 'prepared' is the terminal state — no external verifier link, no instructions beyond apiProofHint ('prepare an unsigned attestation package for an external verifier'), and the Sign button is disabled for these providers, so the journey ends with nothing actionable.
medium_low.fix: Either hide github/email options until the verifier flow exists, or add a 'Continue with external verifier' link (the Morpheus web3auth lane the resolver already advertises) plus copy explaining exactly where to submit the prepared package.

medium_low.title: Degraded runtime silently strips the TEE verification key from built passports
